💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the significant Diablo 4 Developer Update has indeed delivered the goods.
  • You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.
  • Season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the significant Diablo 4 Developer Update has indeed delivered the goods. One of the livestream’s big topics was, of course, the game’s upcoming mini-season, which is set to kick off next week and run until the launch of Lord of Hatred, the game’s anticipated next expansion.

You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.

Season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion. Many of the season’s biggest additions were available to preview in the 2.6.0 Public Test Realm.

It has been revealed that patch 2.6.0, as you might have guessed, is the one that will kick off the slaughter next week. The headline feature here is ability to become The Butcher, the iconic in-game boss who randomly invades players’ games.

Recent findings suggest that when you play as The Butcher, you’ll be rewarded the more kills you get in quick succession. Your skills hotbar will transform to become something more fitting of The Butcher, making them more brutal. You’ll also earn a seasonal currency as you play.

It has been revealed that starting the seasonal questline is how you can begin to assume The Butcher’s form. A Taste of Power can be initiated from Gea Kul. Transforming into The Butcher can be done in a few ways. As you play, you’ll earn Meaty Offerings, which can later be spent on Shrines of Slaughter in the new Helltide. Once activated, the shrine will draw more enemies towards you.

Sources indicate that if you never venture into PvP zones in Diablo 4, this season may change your mind. The standard PvP combat that could only be found in Fields of Hatred has been replaced with a Ceremony of Slaughter, a latest event that rewards you for killing enemies promptly. See it through and The Butcher’s Idol will spawn, allowing you to transform into it.

Elsewhere in the world, you’ll also be able to attain the same power at Slaughterhouses, a new activity type available this season. Inside, you immediately become The Butcher for the entirety of the run.

It has been revealed that the Butcher’s arrival also ties into two of the other Season of Slaughter’s more interesting additions. First, the Killstreak system finally arrives in Diablo 4, rewarding you for being as efficient as possible in carving your way through enemies.

According to recent reports, anyone who played Diablo 3 should be familiar with how it works. It kicks off the moment you get a kill, and has a visible timer where you’ll need continue performing the same action to up your streak. The more kills you get, the more often your timer will refresh.

In a recent development, there are five tiers to climb through: Killstreak, Carnage, Devastation, Bloodbath, and Massacre. You’re awarded for the tier you manage to reach before the timer runs out. You’ll earn XP and seasonal rep each time a Killstreak is achieved.

It has been revealed that the other Butcher-themed addition is Bloodied Items, which is a new item quality available throughout this season. They play into the Killstreak system to grant you even more power. Bloodied Items come with unique affixes that scale off your Killstreak tier. You’ll see many familiar items in that pool, as any item in the game has a chance to drop as Bloodied. Bloodied Items can also be acquired by earning Fresh Meat.

Sources indicate that even if none of that sounds exciting, you’re probably going to redownload the game for The Paladin free trial, which kicks off alongside the new season on March 11. The trial is only available until March 18, and it lets you try out the Paladin class.

The trial is available across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. You’ll be able to take the upcoming class for a spin, but your progress will be capped at level 25. The Paladin can be permanently unlocked by buying the Lord of Hatred expansion, as it’s one of two classes the expansion is introducing.

The good news is that any progress you make in the free trial will carry over to the full game if/when you buy the expansion.

Season of Slaughter also kicks off a Doom: The Dark Ages collaboration event. As we’ve come to expect, there’s a very limited free component to the collaboration, in the form of the Doom Reliquary. This is essentially a mini-battle pass that includes the Shield Saw skin, Slayer’s Flair, the head of the Cyberdemon as a back trophy and various other smaller bits.

The more impressive items - such as character skins, will instead be available to purchase for real money. The list includes the Doom Slayer armor, Mecha Dragon Serrat skin for your cat mount, and a Cacodemon pet.

Though the armor skin is cross-class compatible, judging by how much previous collaboration items have cost in Diablo 4, most of us probably won’t be spending that kind of money to get it.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, declaring a Best Way of Doing Things is a fool’s game, though in recent years my favourite entries in the Tricky Hitting genre – inclusive of soulslikes and their hybridised disciples – have been the significant, bulging ones.
  • Recent findings suggest that even in the latter stages, with a full kit of precisely four ranged spells, Death’s Door is a simple proposition.
  • Sources indicate that still, it’s clever with its limitations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, declaring a Best Way of Doing Things is a fool’s game, though in recent years my favourite entries in the Tricky Hitting genre – inclusive of soulslikes and their hybridised disciples – have been the significant, bulging ones. Elden Rings and Silksongs, with vast kingdoms and deep, rattling toolkits for surviving them. The reason it’s a fool’s game is because you can also have something like Death’s Door, a taut, compact, lighthearted little actioner that fills eight hours instead of 80 and yet never feels underwhelming or compromised for it.

Recent findings suggest that even in the latter stages, with a full kit of precisely four ranged spells, Death’s Door is a simple proposition. You are a crow. You hit things. Occasionally you shoot things. You collect the souls of a frog, a yeti, and a grandmother. Everything in-between directly relates to finding the errant monster/pensioner, or at a stretch, upgrading one of those four abilities.

Sources indicate that still, it’s clever with its limitations. Environments are small in number but vary wildly in tone and texture, and they tightly weave their paths into criss-crossing bundles that maximise travel – evoking the sense of a great, ranging adventure within relatively tiny spaces. The lack of a wiki’s worth of combat options also never becomes a problem, partly because it spreads out its spell unlocks, and partly because the smooth, flowing back-and-forths of its central swordplay are pleasurable enough to carry it anyway. Good bosses, too! They’re all characterful, memorable weirdoes who fight unlike anyone in their minion armies, and usually come with a hidden weakness to deduce and exploit.

It has been revealed that which is welcome, as these big lads and lasses do tend to launch difficulty spikes right up your feathered backside, and do so in a game that isn’t otherwise as fussed about trial-and-error pain endurance as some of its inspirations. They don’t, however, bring the mood down. At times, this tale of a pitch-black soul reaper working as an agent of Death (complete with an office of Death and embittered co-workers of Death) can get downright cosy, leading through you through warmly-lit jungles and breezy waterside ruins.

Recently replaying, I’d also forgotten how witty it can be. Little gaglets are sprinkled throughout, both visual and verbal, but the best jokes are saved for – funnily enough – the bosses, who’ll raise your pre-fight spirit with some amusingly terrible trash talk before becoming the punchline themselves. I audibly wheezed the first time a death animation immediately cut to the foe’s impromptu funeral, their beaked killer among the precious few guests. And even when the joke is recycled later, I couldn’t help tittering at the sight of my enemy – who seconds earlier, had been attempting to fatally sit on me – lying nobly in state.

Sources indicate that I previously considered ending my Valor Mortis review by calling it a gateway into the more demanding side of action-RPGs; a shorter, simpler alternative to FromSoft’s overwhelming titans that might nonetheless serve to introduce curious newcomers to their shared quirks and qualities. The game equivalent of splashing your chest with water before jumping into a pool. In hindsight, Death’s Door was always a better fit for that description, though there’s enough else here you don’t need to be prepping for something tougher to appreciate its lean, keen adventuring.

Skull And Bones Quadruple-A Claims “Puffery,” Say Ubisoft Lawyers

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (382 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thegamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that remember Skull and Bones?
  • In 2025, Jacob Himberger sued Ubisoft in Kansas over allegations of deceptive marketing, arguing that the manufacturer violated the state's consumer protection act.
  • Sources indicate that the lawsuit is two-pronged.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that remember Skull and Bones? It spent 11 years in development and was forgotten the second it launched, as Ubisoft's foray into quadruple-A gaming almost immediately found itself lost at sea. It's hard to be charitable about a game with a $200 million budget that was worse than the then-decade-old Black Flag, and not a notch on its contemporary, Sea of Thieves, but it didn't just face any old ordinary backlash.

In 2025, Jacob Himberger sued Ubisoft in Kansas over allegations of deceptive marketing, arguing that the manufacturer violated the state's consumer protection act.

Sources indicate that the lawsuit is two-pronged. First, it suggests that Ubisoft misled consumers into believing they were buying ownership of the game, rather than a revocable license, highlighting The Crew as an example of server-dependent games becoming unplayable. Secondly, it points to the quadruple-A claim, suggesting that Ubisoft went beyond hype and misled consumers into buying Skull and Bones. However, as reported by Game File, the company's lawyers argue this was "classic puffery.".

According to recent reports, in lawyer-speak, "puffery" means that a claim was not objective advertising and instead exaggerated promotion. Ubisoft argues that when CEO Yves Guillemot described Skull and Bones as "a really full, triple... quadruple-A game, that will deliver in the long run," he was just being a salesman. Though it's also worth noting that the game-maker's misguided pirate RPG was almost its first $70 game, making it distinct from other 'triple-A' titles in its portfolio. Though, these days, you can buy Skull and Bones for $29.99.

It has been revealed that there isn't really a standard idea of what quadruple-A means, but a few studios have thrown the label around to try and signal that their game is truly next-gen and above what other triple-A titles can offer. Xbox, for example, claimed its canceled Perfect Dark reboot was 'AAAA' in job listings, while Dead Space creator Glen Schofield called his spiritual successor The Callisto Protocol an 'AAAA' experience ahead of launch. So, based on that very limited sample, quadruple-A seems to mean canceled or overhyped.

Not exactly the most esteemed firm, and if anything, a signal that you should probably be a bit cautious when a game is marketed as the next big 'AAAA' hit.

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto VI is a game where you spend a lot of time behind the wheel. Always has been. But sometimes, you just won't feel like actively driving, but you also don't to waste money on a cab.

It has been revealed that this is where Auto Drive comes in. It lets the game take over and drive you where you need to go in real time and all with a cinematic camera that shifts and moves, letting you take in the environment without all that pesky "having to pay attention to the road." Red Dead Redemption 2 had the same feature, and I have fond memories of taking advantage of it to watch Arthur ride his horse through that game's incredible environment. It's a great option in GTAVI, but how to use it and turn it on isn't immediately apparent.

First, you must select a destination. Get the GPS set up to direct you to where you want to go.

In a recent development, next, start driving. The Auto Drive is smart, but doesn't seem to be smart enough to make three-point turns or back out of parking lots. You need to be on your way before you can turn it on.

Once you're on the path, hold down in the d-pad and press start to activate Cinematic.

Once you've done this you should be able to hold down the Circle button on PlayStation or the B button on Xbox to activate Auto Drive and... voilà! You can sit back and let Jason or Lucia take the wheel. They will drive legally, even stopping at lights, but you can speed them up if they're taking too long.

I've always enjoyed driving in Grand Theft Auto, but I was grateful to find this almost-hidden option early in the game.

Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Upgrade, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

In a recent development, since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Upgrade to actually see it in action.

Recent findings suggest that the Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

According to recent reports, the Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

Recent findings suggest that the Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

Recent findings suggest that the Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

Warlocks arrive alongside new Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

In a recent development, lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the big day.

#201020. Loneliness is making us sick, but we may be treating it all wrong

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (727 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Loneliness is making us sick, but we may be treating it all wrong

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (727 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, research has established that loneliness can have serious consequences for physical health.
  • Published in Social Problems, the study examines how chronic loneliness and social isolation became recognized as major public health concerns after researchers uncovered links to illness, premature death, and increased healthcare spending.
  • Previous studies highlighted in the research illustrate the severity of these consequences.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, research has established that loneliness can have serious consequences for physical health. However, a newly introduced University of Michigan study warns that treating loneliness primarily as a health problem could shift responsibility away from society and place it on a healthcare system that lacks the tools to restore meaningful social connections.

Published in Social Problems, the study examines how chronic loneliness and social isolation became recognized as major public health concerns after researchers uncovered links to illness, premature death, and increased healthcare spending.

Previous studies highlighted in the research illustrate the severity of these consequences. One estimated that lacking social connections could be as harmful to health as smoking 15 cigarettes a day. Another found that loneliness, social isolation, and living alone were each associated with an approximately 30% higher risk of premature death. The financial burden is also substantial, with separate research estimating that social isolation costs Medicare $6.7 billion each year in care for older adults.

Sources indicate that "Once people saw these findings, they began to treat loneliness as urgent," remarked University of Michigan doctoral student Sofia Hiltner. "But it made me wonder: Why do we only consider problems vital once they are tied to health?".

The Problem With Medicalizing Loneliness.

To understand how loneliness became a medical concern, Hiltner conducted interviews with experts and reviewed more than a decade of media coverage, medical journal articles, and academic literature.

Her analysis revealed that establishing a connection between loneliness and poor health helped the issue gain credibility. However, it also encouraged what she describes as a "logical leap": the belief that any problem affecting human health should become the responsibility of the healthcare system.

"Not everything that relates to health belongs in healthcare," she said. "Doctors can screen patients and connect them to services, but they cannot rebuild communities or shorten work hours.".

Hiltner, a predoctoral trainee in social demography at the Population Studies Center within the University of Michigan's Institute for Social Research, was inspired to investigate loneliness after witnessing her grandmother become increasingly isolated as she aged.

When Hiltner entered graduate school to research social isolation among older adults, she learned that clinical trials were investigating a "loneliness pill." The discovery prompted her to question why loneliness was being approached primarily as a medical condition rather than a social problem.

"After my grandfather died, my grandmother lived alone and there was little structure in her life," Hiltner noted. "She didn't seem to have many friends or activities. It made me think about everything that happened throughout her life that led to that point. I wondered about the social policies, in addition to dynamics at the family level, that could have helped prevent that situation.".

Finding Solutions Beyond the Healthcare System.

Recent findings suggest that interestingly, Hiltner found that the medical community was initially reluctant to take responsibility for addressing loneliness. Much of the momentum behind incorporating loneliness into healthcare instead came from academic researchers, government health officials, and insurance companies.

Although recognizing loneliness as a medical concern can generate greater awareness and encourage intervention, it may also divert valuable resources from efforts to address the social circumstances that leave people isolated.

Recent findings suggest that "There is the risk that defining loneliness as medical crowds out other ways of responding to the problem," she said. "Attention, time and resources are limited. On the other hand, framing it as medical may inspire more action than would have otherwise happened.".

Hiltner hopes her findings will encourage policymakers to reconsider how they define social problems and explore preventive strategies that address their underlying causes before they develop into serious health concerns.

"I would like them to reflect on the strengths and limitations of addressing problems through the healthcare system, and look farther upstream to understand how a problem emerges, considering ways to intervene before it occurs," she mentioned. "Healthcare can help, but it can only go so far.".

Those starting scenarios range from peddling human meat to running the finest cyber-frappucino stall this side of Tannhäuser Gate. There are no hard release dates, and the contents of each revision may alter, but developers Questing Goose Studio have shared some rough timeframes.

Late January is when you'll "very likely" get the chance to be an Organ Dealer, care of the second major update. "Players will start by buying different organs and fulfilling specific requests, and will later be able to grow or print organs," a Steam blog explains. You'll also be able to filter blood and remove diseases, with different blood types having different value modifiers. How will you get your hands on organs? By sending horrible black market thugs on foraging "expeditions".

Sources indicate that last but not least, the planned April update will add the Street Food Vendor starting scenario. This lets you weave a livelihood around choice beverages and edibles from a range of cultures, supported by updates to the game's Aquaculture and Hydroponics tech. Sounds a lot cheerier than the organ trading racket, but then again, Probably Stolen will doubtless find a way to make it utterly grim. Guests at Sweeney's Cantina know better than to ask what our frappucinos are made of.

In a recent development, are you playing Probably Stolen? It's been doing better than expected. I was keen on the demo, but my attention was lured away by a truly upsetting game about dogpeople in caves.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that after a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next significant game has officially rolled out.
  • The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that after a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next significant game has officially rolled out. Marathon, the extraction shooter from the studio behind Destiny, has managed to find a decent, if a little small of an audience.

The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.

Industry observers note that the open test was largely well-received, and players actually revealed up for it. It peaked at a very respectable 143,621 concurrent players on Steam, which put it within striking distance of the peak concurrent of its chief competitor, Arc Raiders - at least when you compare both of their pre-launch Server Slam events.

In a recent development, in Arc Raiders’ case, those figures were far outpaced at the game’s actual launch, and the Embark shooter continues to command a very active player base to this day. A paid product garnering far more players than the same product’s own free sampler is never not a good sign, so many hoped something similar would happen with Marathon.

Marathon has now officially released, and it doesn’t look like it managed to pull an Arc Raiders - at least so far. At its peak, the Bungie shooter attracted 88,337 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), which is a little over half of its Server Slam’s 143,621 peak concurrent.

In a recent development, numbers have, of course, dropped since then, which is normal, as players log off for the night. This is obviously not the end of the road for Marathon. Friday, and the weekend, may well push numbers closer to the Server Slam heights.

It has been revealed that indeed, word of mouth is quite positive, with the game currently sitting at a Very Positive user review rating on Steam, based on over 4,600 reviews. As has been proven time and time again in recent years, nothing catapults a game like players emphatically advocating for it to their friends, so it could simply be that mainstream players are cautious.

It will become clear where things settle over the weekend.

The playoffs are being held online by Riot Games and JioBLAST. Series in the bracket are played as best-of-three or best-of-five.

According to recent reports, godLike arrived in form. They reached the playoffs with an unbeaten 4-0 record in the open qualifier, VLR.gg reported. They shared joint first to fourth place in that event, which ran from 17 to 20 November. Trigger Point finished in the group placed fifth to eighth.

GodLike fielded Karam1L, Paradox and RvK from India, alongside sayoo from Indonesia and azyshaha from the Philippines. Sabyasachi ‘Antidote’ Bose is listed as head coach, with Samar as substitute. Trigger Point’s listed players are SangraM, WEELJACK and RaJ.

It has been revealed that south Asian teams cannot qualify directly for Kickoff. The top two from the playoffs join the Oceania playoff winner and the Southeast Asia playoff runner-up in a four-team Last Chance Qualifier. Only its winner goes through to Kickoff in Bangkok, according to Dot Esports.

The stakes are high. Twelve teams will play at Kickoff, and the top three will qualify for Masters 1. The route stays narrow later in the season too. South Asia has no direct place at the Cups, with Cup 1 in Manila and Cup 2 in Tokyo. It sends two teams to an eight-team Pacific LCQ, and the winner takes the last Cup place.

According to recent reports, the qualifier also has a new organiser. Riot picked JioBLAST to run the South Asia qualifiers instead of NODWIN Gaming, the previous organiser. Riot has not said why it made the change.

According to recent reports, the UK interest lies with SIGN Esports. They beat Zexar Esports 2-0 in another upper bracket quarter-final. Russel ‘Russ’ Mendes joined SIGN Esports on 16 November 2026. He is the only player from the UK in the eight-team playoff field.

Russ was born in 1998 and is of Indian descent. He won the VALORANT Challengers 2025 South Asia Grand Final with Velocity Gaming on 13 July 2025, when they beat S8UL 3-1.

In a recent development, godLike Esports and SIGN Esports both remain in the upper bracket, one defeat away from the lower bracket. Trigger Point Esports and Zexar Esports must win from the lower bracket to stay in contention for a top-two finish. The playoffs run until 29 November 2026.

#201013. Xenogears Is Finally Getting Remastered, But Not in the Way You Think

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (793 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

Xenogears Is Finally Getting Remastered, But Not in the Way You Think

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (793 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that there are two perspectives on remasters and remakes.
  • Recent findings suggest that to be fair, three Xenogears remasters are currently being developed by fans, each with its own codename: Weltall, Exodus, and Atlas.
  • In a recent development, the project could hardly be called a Xenogears remaster if it didn't include notable upgrades over the original.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that there are two perspectives on remasters and remakes. On one hand, we have those who complain whenever a developer unveils a newly introduced one, wishing they would dedicate development efforts to bringing new IPs to life. On the other hand, we have those who rejoice and feel the nostalgia tingling whenever a game that shaped their tastes returns to the modern era. I fall into the latter camp, which is why I am extremely excited for the upcoming fanmade remaster of Xenogears.

Recent findings suggest that to be fair, three Xenogears remasters are currently being developed by fans, each with its own codename: Weltall, Exodus, and Atlas. Today I'll discuss the Atlas remaster because it seems to be the one the fanbase is most excited about, and it already has an imminent release date of 15 December 2026. However, keep in mind that since this is not an official remaster from Square Enix, you can only legally play it if you own an original copy of Xenogears at home.

In a recent development, the project could hardly be called a Xenogears remaster if it didn't include notable upgrades over the original. According to the creator, Reddit user Ok-Bed3203, the entire game has been rebuilt in the Godot engine and will run directly inside it, provided you supply your own copy of the game. Fans can experience Xenogears Atlas in two distinct visual styles, dubbed Canon and HD.

Recent findings suggest that in Canon mode, the visuals remain faithful to the 1998 release, while incorporating technical fixes such as eliminating flickering triangles or textures, stabilizing sprites and images, and smoothing out screen fades. Meanwhile, High Definition mode introduces enhanced textures and sprites, 16:9 widescreen support (with menus, text, and FMVs preserved in their original 4:3 framing so nothing gets stretched), updated lighting and visual effects, and 3D Gears.

Both modes will support 60 FPS, 120 FPS, or your monitor's native refresh rate. They also include 2K CG cutscenes upscaled by Laichzeit (likely exclusive to HD mode, though not explicitly specified), subtitles in every language, fan translations, and quality-of-life options like text speed adjustments, quick loads, full-screen or windowed modes, and automatic pausing when running in the background.

According to recent reports, after the initial release, the developers plan to add a Mods menu that lets you load custom text patches and swap images or audio files by name, along with remastered music from Xenogears' iconic soundtrack and further touch-ups to the 2K movies. The community has also suggested several additions right now under consideration, including random encounter rate toggles, a reduced-flash mode, auto-advancing dialogue, optional voice-over via the Spoken Mirror fan dub (slated to arrive alongside the Disc 2 remake), and a dedicated Android port.

Sources indicate that as you probably noticed, the developer mentioned a Disc 2 remake. That sounds like a tall order, because as anyone who played the game remembers, Xenogears features a pristine Disc 1, whereas the second disc was famously rushed after Square cut the budget before the project could be finished, which severely undermined the experience. Atlas aims to give Disc 2 the breathing room it never received. While it is not yet completely clear what that will entail or when it will arrive, it is easily the most intriguing prospect of this entire fanmade remaster.

According to recent reports, while the project looks incredible and has me thoroughly hyped, one looming question always hangs in the air these days: was this project made using AI? The developer preemptively addressed that very concern:.

“About AI, since it always comes up: yes, I used AI as a tool along the way, and I'm not going to pretend otherwise. But this is not a vibe-coded project. I checked every cutscene, every movement and every 16:9 margin by hand, then fixed it and compared it with the original. A huge part of the work was the boring part: tracking down the smallest glitches left over from the PS1 renderer, one by one, until they were gone. Monk work, honestly. I hope you'll feel it when you play.”.

About AI, since it always comes up: yes, I used AI as a tool along the way, and I'm not going to pretend otherwise.

So there you have it. If you want to experience or revisit Xenogears with revamped visuals, quality-of-life additions, tweaks, and technical fixes, Xenogears Atlas might just be the way to go. This Xenogears remaster rolls out on 15 December 2026, via Godot for PC, though you will still need your original copy to get it running. Who knows, maybe this will finally wake Square Enix up to greenlight a full-fledged official remaster, or at least sell the IP back to Tetsuya Takahashi.

Common supplements rival antibiotics in treating severe gum disease

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1549 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A familiar dietary supplement combined with low-dose aspirin may offer an unexpected alternative to antibiotics for people with severe gum disease.
  • The findings, published in the Journal of Periodontology, come from researchers affiliated with Albert Einstein Israelite Hospital, Guarulhos University (UNG), the University of Taubaté (UNITAU), and the Ribeirão Preto School of Dentistry at USP (FORP-USP) in Brazil, as well as Harvard University in the United States.
  • The study suggests that combining omega-3 with low-dose acetylsalicylic acid (ASA), better known as aspirin, could reduce the need for antibiotics in certain patients.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A familiar dietary supplement combined with low-dose aspirin may offer an unexpected alternative to antibiotics for people with severe gum disease. In a year-long clinical trial, patients who received omega-3 and aspirin alongside conventional periodontal treatment experienced nearly identical clinical benefits to those who received antibiotics. Perhaps even more surprisingly, the improvements were still evident six months after supplementation ended.

The findings, published in the Journal of Periodontology, come from researchers affiliated with Albert Einstein Israelite Hospital, Guarulhos University (UNG), the University of Taubaté (UNITAU), and the Ribeirão Preto School of Dentistry at USP (FORP-USP) in Brazil, as well as Harvard University in the United States.

The study suggests that combining omega-3 with low-dose acetylsalicylic acid (ASA), better known as aspirin, could reduce the need for antibiotics in certain patients. The discovery is particularly timely given growing worldwide concerns about antibiotic resistance, which occurs when bacteria develop the ability to survive exposure to drugs designed to kill them.

Why Severe Gum Disease Is So Difficult To Treat.

In a recent development, researchers monitored 109 patients with advanced periodontitis over 12 months. Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease that develops when bacteria accumulate below the gumline, triggering an immune response that can gradually damage the tissues and bone that hold teeth in place. Without proper treatment, the disease can cause teeth to loosen and eventually fall out.

It has been revealed that as periodontitis progresses, spaces known as periodontal pockets form between the teeth and gums. These pockets can become increasingly deep, making it difficult to remove harmful bacteria through ordinary brushing and flossing.

According to recent reports, "Patients with severe disease have very deep pockets, which act as reservoirs for bacteria associated with the disease. It's a very challenging condition to treat," says dental surgeon Nídia Cristina Castro dos Santos, the first author of the study and a professor and researcher at Einstein.

Putting Omega-3 and Aspirin to the Test.

The researchers randomly divided the participants into four treatment groups. Every patient received subgingival instrumentation, commonly referred to as scaling. This standard periodontal treatment involves removing bacterial deposits and hardened plaque from tooth surfaces beneath the gums. Each group also received a different complementary treatment.

Patients in the control group received inactive substitutes for the antibiotics, omega-3, and aspirin, supplied in capsules that looked identical to those containing the active treatments.

A second group received metronidazole and amoxicillin three times daily for 14 days. This combination of antibiotics has some of the strongest scientific evidence supporting its use as an additional treatment for severe periodontitis.

Participants in the third group took three grams of omega-3 each day, together with a daily dose of low-dose aspirin, for six months. The fourth group received both interventions, taking antibiotics for two weeks while following the six-month omega-3 and aspirin regimen.

The researchers assessed the patients' progress at three, six, and 12 months.

Omega-3 and Aspirin Rival Antibiotics.

At the end of the study, approximately 58% of patients in the antibiotic group had reached the researchers' clinical treatment target, defined as having no more than four remaining deep periodontal pockets.

The omega-3 and aspirin group achieved an almost identical success rate of 57.7%. By comparison, only 23.1% of patients who underwent scaling and received placebos reached the same target. Interestingly, administering both antibiotics and the omega-3 and aspirin regimen together did not produce any additional benefits.

Although antibiotics can improve treatment outcomes in patients with particularly severe gum disease, they are not routinely necessary for everyone with periodontitis.

It has been revealed that "The use of antibiotics isn't considered the gold standard of treatment. Although metronidazole and amoxicillin yield good results in the most severe cases, their use should be evaluated on a case-by-case basis due to risks related to bacterial resistance and possible adverse effects," states Castro dos Santos.

Helping the Body Naturally Resolve Inflammation.

The findings build on earlier research into the potential role of omega-3 fatty acids in protecting oral health. In a previous investigation, also supported by FAPESP and published in Scientific Reports, scientists found that omega-3 supplementation reduced periodontal inflammation and bone loss in rats. The protective effects were particularly notable when supplementation was combined with physical exercise.

Although results from animal studies do not necessarily translate directly to humans, the earlier findings provided clues that omega-3 might help regulate the inflammatory processes that contribute to gum disease.

Omega-3 fatty acids are a group of fats found in foods such as oily fish and are widely available as dietary supplements. Beyond their nutritional importance, they serve as building blocks for certain molecules that help regulate inflammation.

Industry observers note that castro explains that omega-3 works differently from conventional anti-inflammatory medications. Instead of simply interfering with pathways that promote inflammation, omega-3 helps the body produce molecules involved in bringing inflammation to a natural conclusion and supporting tissue repair.

Industry observers note that this process, known as the resolution of inflammation, is an active biological mechanism that helps the body return to normal after an immune response. In chronic inflammatory diseases such as periodontitis, inflammation can persist and contribute to ongoing tissue damage.

In a recent development, the researchers included low-dose aspirin because it can promote the formation of certain inflammation-resolving molecules. They suspected that combining aspirin with omega-3 could strengthen the body's ability to control the persistent inflammation associated with advanced gum disease.

Benefits That Lasted Beyond Treatment.

According to recent reports, the researchers had originally expected antibiotics and the omega-3 regimen to work best when administered together. Instead, the findings revealed that targeting inflammation could produce clinical improvements comparable to those achieved through antibiotic treatment.

Recent findings suggest that "We imagined that the combination of antibiotics and omega-3 would be most effective in controlling periodontitis in these patients. We also believed that the results for the group that used omega-3 with ASA would be slightly lower than those for the antibiotic group. The result was surprising because the two therapies performed very similarly, paving the way for it to become a treatment option for these patients," claims Castro.

Equally intriguing was how long the improvements lasted. Six months after patients stopped taking omega-3 and aspirin, their clinical outcomes remained similar to those observed when the treatment ended.

According to Castro, this persistence raises the possibility that adjusting the body's inflammatory response could have lasting therapeutic effects. However, scientists are still working to understand the biological mechanisms responsible.

A Potential Alternative Amid Rising Antibiotic Resistance.

For dental surgeon Magda Feres, the study's lead author and a full professor at the Harvard School of Dental Medicine and the Graduate Program in Dentistry at UNG, targeting the body's inflammatory response could provide a valuable treatment option for certain patients.

"The combination of omega-3 and low-dose aspirin achieved clinical benefits comparable to those of the metronidazole and amoxicillin protocol, opening up a real alternative for those who can't take antibiotics, especially patients with allergies or intolerance to these medications," she indicates.

The potential to reduce antibiotic use has implications that extend well beyond dentistry. Antibiotic resistance ranks among the greatest threats to global public health, making it increasingly important to identify effective treatment strategies that do not depend on these medications.

"Demonstrating that it's possible to treat severe periodontitis by modulating the body's own response is newly introduced and relevant information that helps preserve antibiotics for when they are truly indispensable," indicates Feres.

More Research Is Needed Before Clinical Practice Changes.

Recent findings suggest that despite the encouraging findings, the researchers caution that the results are not sufficient to justify an immediate change in how dentists treat severe periodontitis. The participants did not have other significant systemic or oral diseases, meaning the results may not apply equally to patients with additional health conditions.

Larger studies involving more diverse populations will be needed to validate the findings and determine which patients are most likely to benefit from each treatment strategy.

It is also important to recognize that omega-3 and aspirin were used alongside professional periodontal treatment, rather than as a substitute for it. Aspirin carries potential risks, including an increased risk of bleeding, and may not be appropriate for everyone.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, Feres and her colleagues are investigating how the different treatments affect the communities of bacteria living inside periodontal pockets. Early microbiological findings point to a decline in bacterial species associated with periodontal disease and an increase in microorganisms linked to healthier gums.

These ongoing investigations could help explain why targeting inflammation produced such promising results and whether the approach can reliably benefit a broader range of patients.

"It's an key step forward, but not the end of the story. Therefore, the message is one of cautious optimism: we have a promising, scientifically plausible alternative to antibiotics in select cases. Routine replacement will require more evidence," she concludes.

  • Today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3. The developer has been releasing regular updates for the action RPG since its launch in early February. Earlier patches have addressed major bugs like healing item use inconsistencies, and more have arrived since to tackle various balance and loot-related problems.

Today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB. There’s plenty here worth getting excited about, so let’s dig in.

Recent findings suggest that to begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai. When Nioh 3 reached one million sales, Team Ninja said it would gift every player the Thunderous set in celebration, and the set’s two variants are now available in-game.

In a recent development, the more interesting side of the patch is, unsurprisingly, its change log. There appears to be a focus on online co-op and AI summons in this one, with various tweaks to the make the process more rewarding, and, in some cases, worthwhile.

The amount of Glory obtained when you complete a mission in multiplayer has been increased, regardless of which player was the host. The other major change mainly affects AI Benevolent Grave summons, making it so bosses will no longer target a single player for almost the entirety of the fight.

While summoning AI helpers has always been useful in Nioh 3, they didn’t always help in boss fights, specifically because the boss tended to focus on the player who summoned them, leaving the AI to run around eating AoE hits before dying.

It has been revealed that patch 1.04 makes a couple of welcome gameplay tweaks to the feel of combat. Ninjutsu, and Onmyo Magic will now hit their targets more consistently in situations where there’s a difference in elevation between the player and the enemy.

According to recent reports, in the same vein, you’ll now be able to attack (quick/strong) right after jumping, which removes the pause that previously buffered the attack instead. This could mean even more air combos that don’t specifically require Martial Arts.

Sources indicate that you can look forward to a couple of quality of life tweaks in this patch, too, such as the change that allows the game to automatically send any Sudama Soul Cores dropped by merchants to your item box. This happens from the second one onwards, which means you won’t have to pick half a dozen each time you go to sell a batch of items.

Speaking of the item box, the limit of forging materials has been increased for some of them. If you’ve been running Battle Scroll missions and Expeditions for gear, you’ll be happy to know that you can now exit the session from the main menu directly.

There’s plenty more to patch 1.04, including fixes and balance tweaks for several weapons, such as Samurai dual swords, odachi, and more for a few Ninja weapons, too. The patch also brings several bug fixes to the game.

You can read the full set of patch notes on Steam.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, hollow Knight: Silksong was practically the GTA 6 for indie games.
  • So, Aeternum Game Studios delayed Aeterna Lucis by an entire year to steer clear, only to end up launching on the same day as Cherry Time — the showcase dedicated to Silksong's upcoming DLC.
  • A little over a year ago, just as we were about to launch our game, you announced Silksong," the studio mentioned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, hollow Knight: Silksong was practically the GTA 6 for indie games. Nearly a decade of development, enough hype to send an entire community into an ouroboros of gaslighting, and so many copies sold at launch that it crashed Steam and the Nintendo eShop; releasing a game on the same day, especially a metroidvania, was a death sentence.

So, Aeternum Game Studios delayed Aeterna Lucis by an entire year to steer clear, only to end up launching on the same day as Cherry Time — the showcase dedicated to Silksong's upcoming DLC.

"Dear Team Cherry. A little over a year ago, just as we were about to launch our game, you announced Silksong," the studio mentioned. "We stepped aside, pushed the whole project back a year and, honestly, it was one of the best decisions we've ever made: the genre had an incredible year, and we got to enjoy Silksong as fans and polish Aeterna Lucis into the game we always dreamed it would be.

"Now here we are again, just days from launch. Aeterna Lucis, our new metroidvania, comes out on December 3... and you announce Cherry Time," it continued. "This time we're staying put. Not to go against you, but because a lot of people have been waiting for the Queen of Light for a long time, and we don't want to make them wait any longer. Whatever happens on Thursday, we'll be watching like any other fan. And if Sea of Sorrow ends up landing on the same day, the real winners will be metroidvania fans.".

In a recent development, there's been a bit of hubbub on Twitter about whether Team Cherry should offer a courtesy to indie developers privately due to the sheer popularity of its games, but Aeternum has shut down those kinds of comments and assured that this statement is all in good fun. "Thanks to everyone who took this with the same humor we wrote it with," they commented. "If fate insists, let the king and the queen go to the ball together, we're ready.".

According to recent reports, and, as some fans pointed out, Team Cherry did tease post-launch content stretching into 2026, but the timing almost makes me think that somebody put a curse on Aeternum Game Studios. Almost. "We have to ask, with all the love in the world: is it just us, or does the universe have it in for us?" the team mused. "And since you're about to wreck our lives all over again, the least we can do is make a bundle together.".

I'd be remiss not to mention that you can wishlist Aeterna Lucis here. There's even a demo available right now if you want to give the game a go before buying it. Sea of Sorrow is completely free, so if you have a spare chunk of change, Aeternum Game Studio's newest release is at least worth considering — especially with how rotten their luck has been.

It has been revealed that A big part of the point of The Blood of Dawnwalker is that you're on a fixed time limit. You've got 30 in-game days and nights to try and save your family, and if you don't manage to see everything the game has to offer, well, the game's director is fine with that. But that doesn't matter as much now, as The Blood of Dawnwalker is getting its 1.2 patch next week that adds in a fresh game plus mode.

According to recent reports, "If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with New Game+!" a post from the devs explains. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over; the level cap will be raised to 100; enemies will be balanced and scale uniformly across all regions; and items will have NG+ versions with updated stats." Sounds like your usual new game plus affair! I suppose it is a good opportunity to try out different things compared to your first playthrough, but I'm not exactly aligned with the idea that the timer restriction is too restricting (as some mods have made clear how others feel that way).

In any case, the revision goes a tad further than that. If you got the Eclipse Edition of the game, the in-game soundtrack that came with it "will be extended with additional songs from the game." You can expect the soundtrack on streaming services soon, too. While details are slimmer here, there are also some planned balance changes, like updated enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat, and terrain geometry has seen some improvements to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration.".

According to recent reports, overall, a bit of a smaller update compared to the last one, but one I'm sure will be welcome to some all the same. If you've not had a chance to check the game out yet and still feel on the fence about it, here's some lovely words from Mark's review: "There’s always that sense that something important or unexpected could be lurking around the next corner, to pull you into a quest dripping with depth and intrigue. It works to ensure the more busywork-esque tasks attached to angering Brencis and his Boyars never make Vale Sangora feel home to a string of boring boxes to tick. It’s a vibrant, constantly changing place with a thousand different threads metaphorically criss-crossing just beneath its surface, just as ancient ruins literally criss-cross beneath its swamps, crags, and forests.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GOC Esports took the opening map, but Revenant XSpark won the next two to reach the upper semi-final of the VCT Pacific Kickoff South Asia qualifier playoffs. Kryon Esports are next, with two South Asian places in the Pacific Last Chance Qualifier at stake.

The third upper-bracket quarter-final of the VCT Pacific Kickoff: South Asia – Qualifier 2027 needed a deciding third map.

Sunset ran for 51 minutes. Revenant XSpark levelled by winning Haven 13-5 in 35 minutes. They then won the deciding map, which lasted 49 minutes.

The scoreline matches the two sides’ Predator League India semi-final, which Revenant XSpark also won 2-1. GOC lost the third-place match of that event to GodLike Esports. GOC now drop into the lower bracket and face RANKERS in the first lower round on Wednesday 25 November.

Sources indicate that kryon booked their place in the upper semi-final by beating RANKERS 2-1. On the other side of the upper bracket, GodLike Esports beat Trigger Point Esports 2-0 and SIGN Esports beat Zexar Esports by the same score.

Second place in that Predator League event earned Kryon 125,000 INR, while the winners collected 250,000 INR, VLR.gg reported. Both teams qualified for the APAC Predator League 2027, an offline event in Ho Chi Minh City.

Revenant XSpark played the Predator League with Lightningfast, hellff, Hoax, deecee and Venka. Rinsat, now listed on Revenant XSpark’s roster alongside Hoax, Techno, venka, k1ngkappa and Madelyn, appeared in Kryon’s lineup for that event.

Riot Games and JioBLAST are running the playoffs online as an eight-team double-elimination bracket from 23 to 29 November. The field came through an online Open Qualifier of 152 teams, held from 17 to 20 November. Revenant XSpark finished in the top four there, while GOC placed in the 5th–8th group.

It has been revealed that the South Asian qualifiers will be joined at the Last Chance Qualifier by one team from Oceania and the runner-up of the SEA Kickoff Playoffs. ONE Up is organising that event with Riot Games.

The thriller goes our away. 2-1 vs GOC 🐺⚡️#WolvenSpark pic.twitter.com/MOvm1X70sH.

— Revenant Esports (@RevenantGGWP) November 24, 2026.

Beyond it lies the 2027 Pacific Kickoff in Bangkok, from 11 to 31 January 2027. It will feature 12 teams: eight partner teams and four Open teams. The top three qualify for the first Masters event, Masters Seoul. Any Open team that reaches Kickoff receives a fixed US$100,000 per event on top of any prize money.

The winner of Thursday’s match plays in the upper final on 27 November, and the grand final is on 29 November.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Sims 4 will soon get a fresh revision to resolve a number of complications, some of which have long caused headaches for players. The latest update will arrive March 17 on PC and Mac, followed by PlayStation and Xbox at an unspecified time later.

Outside of the fixes themselves, the patch also makes good on the recent re-commitment to continue improving quality of life for players, so there’s plenty here longtime players will appreciate.

In the latest episode of The Sims 4’s Laundry List blog series, where the developer goes through the most reported problems with the game and how it prepares to solve them, we got a rundown of what to expect from next week’s patch.

You can look forward to five major fixes in this one, but arguably the most vital is a change to how Sims determine who they speak with on a lot. This is especially relevant for public lots, where Sims would sometimes interrupt ongoing conversations by barging in and starting a conversation with your Sim.

Going forward, Sims will prioritise familiar Sims with whom they already have rapport, and be less likely to latch onto strangers. If you’ve witnessed a date your Sim was on get interrupted because of that, you’ll certainly appreciate the change.

It has been revealed that speaking of budding romance, Prom is coming back to in-game Calendars, and Sims can once again attend. Maxis said this will work with newly introduced and existing saves, and that you should also expect Prom goals to be completable once again.

It has been revealed that pets and animals get some love in this patch, too. First, pets and horses will no longer get lost in Premade Households. The fix prevents that from happening in newly introduced saves, but if you already had that happen to you in your current save, it’ll still be there.

Industry observers note that you may now also assign animals to an Animal Shed after moving your house to a latest lot, so you hopefully won’t be confused as to why they’re stuck in your inventory. This fix applies to existing saves as well as new ones.

Recent findings suggest that lower down the list of urgent fixes is an patch that makes it so Sims’ eye blinking will show fully closed eyes for most interactions. The upcoming patch also comes with a host of Sims autonomy fixes, including one that prevents them from excessively flirting with each other.

Industry observers note that catch up on the full list at the link near the top of the page. And, in case you missed it, Maxis recently confirmed that The Sims 4 will soon get paid mods, something that many in the community are skeptical about.

In a recent development, earlier this year in a bit of a shakeup for the fleshiest kid in town, Super Meat Boy entered into a new dimension in the aptly named Super Meat Boy 3D. I've not played it but it seems like a good take on the format. Clearly, though, sometimes you just need to play the hits, as a new release of the original game is on the way in the form of Super Meat Boy Again+, a remaster with updated graphics, levels and plenty more.

What is there is very clearly Super Meat Boy, uh, again, just with a massive latest lick of paint. There is probably some kind of joke to be made about it being DLSS yassified, but I'm too tired to think of one, so, you get the point. But it does look pretty good! I do kind of miss the Flash game aesthetic, I think there's a real charm to the sort of visual design sensibilities you'd find from that era, but this remaster certainly ain't ugly at least. Apparently it's not just the art that's new, as there's also new music, cutscenes, secrets and "stuff.".

Sources indicate that if the animated sequences featured in the trailer, which you can have a gander at above, are included in the final game that'll be a treat to watch too, as I think they better capture the Newgrounds pseudo sub-genre of animation than the graphical overhaul. It sounds like they will be looking at the Steam page, so, a treat to look forward to while committing an act of masochism by playing it!

According to recent reports, there's no release date attached to this remaster, so we'll all just have to sit tight for an revision there. The original is still listed on Steam, but if you fancy as big a dose of nostalgia as the trailer is trying to present to you, you could always go play the original, plain old regular Meat Boy. It's playable right on Newgrounds thanks to the Flash emulator Ruffle and works like a dream! Or if you're happy to wait, you could always wishlist the fresh one on Steam.

10 Fighting Games That Totally Reinvent Themselves Halfway Through

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1574 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I am a full-time fighting game enthusiast.
  • According to recent reports, having played countless fighting games over the years, a handful stand out for how dramatically they shift their rules, mechanics, or entire structure mid-match, mid-mode, or halfway through a campaign.
  • Recent findings suggest that I grew up alongside Goku and his friends, sinking hundreds of hours into every Dragon Ball game on the PlayStation 2 and PS4.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I am a full-time fighting game enthusiast. I thrive on those intense, white-knuckle matches that push my skills to the limit—even when I have to retry a tough fight over and over. Honestly, half the magic lies in that process of adapting until you finally break through the wall. Beyond pure mechanics, though, I have a special soft spot for titles that refuse to stay boxed in, introducing new rules and systems as you progress until they practically reinvent themselves halfway through.

According to recent reports, having played countless fighting games over the years, a handful stand out for how dramatically they shift their rules, mechanics, or entire structure mid-match, mid-mode, or halfway through a campaign. They genuinely caught me off guard when I first played them, keeping the experience fresh instead of letting it settle into a predictable loop. Here are 10 fighting games that pull off that kind of reinvention, ranked from the cleverest twists to the most radical genre-bending shifts.

Recent findings suggest that I grew up alongside Goku and his friends, sinking hundreds of hours into every Dragon Ball game on the PlayStation 2 and PS4. Naturally, I nearly teared up with excitement when Dragon Ball: Sparking! ZERO was revealed—and once I finally got my hands on it, the combat immediately won me over, recapturing the spirit of Dragon Ball Z: Budokai Tenkaichi 3 with sharper visuals and an expanded roster.

According to recent reports, as I dove deeper into its Episode Battle campaign, however, I realized it wasn't just retreading familiar manga and anime arcs. By fulfilling specific hidden objectives mid-fight—like defeating an opponent within a strict time limit or making an unexpected choice—you unlock Sparking! Episodes, which act as full-fledged "What If?" timelines that rewrite the rest of that character's campaign. Seeing the story branch off into uncharted territory made clearing the main mode feel far more exciting than simply replaying the same plot beats we all know by heart.

I have been a die-hard fan of Jin Kazama's saga ever since I first booted up Tekken 3 on the original PlayStation, and I've played nearly every entry since—including Tekken 7 on PS4 (following its 2015 arcade debut). Beyond bringing an expanded roster and memorable newcomers to the table, it also shook up the formula halfway through its main story campaign to give the climax far more dramatic weight.

Industry observers note that throughout the first half of The Mishima Saga, the game sticks to the series' classic blueprint: straightforward one-on-one bouts fought under standard Tekken rules. Once Heihachi reclaims the Mishima Zaibatsu in the second half, though, the campaign throws traditional tournament rules out the window in favor of boss encounters featuring super armor phases, special EX and Rage meters, health regeneration, and mid-fight Quick-Time Events that turn battles into cinematic spectacles. Those mechanics completely changed how I approached the late-game fights, forcing me to play much more defensively so I wouldn't enter the next phase with a depleted health bar.

Mortal Kombat is another legendary franchise that has delivered decades of over-the-top violence, though narrative fatigue and identity complications eventually pushed NetherRealm Studios to hit the reset button with Mortal Kombat 1.

In a recent development, I placed Mortal Kombat 1 here because of how dramatically it flips both its narrative tone and its opponent design in the final stretch of its Story Mode. Across the first 14 chapters, the campaign presents a relatively grounded reboot centered on martial arts tournaments and political intrigue within Liu Kang's Newly introduced Era.

According to recent reports, once the story reaches its climax at the Pyramid of Argus, however, the multiverse blows wide open and pits you against procedurally generated hybrid fighters that mash up the appearances, special moves, and Fatalities of two different characters into one. Facing off against unpredictable fusions completely changes how you read opponents on the fly, turning the finale into a chaotic, anything-goes brawl.

Sources indicate that another absolute favorite from my old PS2 days—and one I would love to see get a proper remake or sequel—is Def Jam: Fight for NY. It let you build your own custom brawler and drop straight into a gritty turf war packed with betrayals, brutal environmental knockouts, and some of the biggest hip-hop icons of the era.

In a recent development, what really hooked me in its Story Mode was how your moveset evolves halfway through the climb. You start by creating your fighter and picking a single base discipline from five options: Martial Arts, Wrestling, Submissions, Kickboxing, or Streetfighting. Later on, by training at Stapleton Athletics gym, you unlock the ability to buy and fuse up to three distinct fighting styles onto your character—completely rewriting your combo strings, counters, and Blazin' finishers depending on the exact styles you combine.

It has been revealed that you can't talk about standout modern fighting games without bringing up Street Fighter 6, a title I have easily poured dozens of hours into. Much like the other entries on this list, its single-player journey gradually reinvents itself into something far wilder than its opening hours suggest.

Early on in World Tour, you control a rookie avatar roaming Metro City with a bare-bones moveset while learning the fundamentals of the Drive System. Once you travel to Nayshall and start training under multiple Masters from the main roster, however, the mode opens up into a full-blown hybrid moveset sandbox. Before long, you can mix and match special moves from completely incompatible archetypes—pairing Ryu's Hadoken with Zangief's Spinning Piledriver and Chun-Li's kicks—exclusively within World Tour and the Battle Hub.

Unlike most games on this list, Nidhogg reinvents its genre dynamically in the middle of every single match. Each bout begins in the center of the stage as a tense, minimalist one-on-one fencing duel where spacing, blade height, and timely disarms mean everything.

Sources indicate that the moment one player scores a kill, though, the game instantly mutates from a methodical duel into a frantic obstacle-course platformer. The winner has to sprint across multiple screens toward their goal while the defeated player repeatedly respawns ahead to stop them using any dirty trick available—from dive kicks to throwing their sword—flipping attacker and defender roles back and forth until someone finally reaches the end to be devoured by the giant Nidhogg worm.

As we climb closer to the top spot, the mid-game transformations become much more drastic. At its core, For Honor is built around its Art of Battle directional guard system, demanding careful reads in close-quarters melee duels—and in its large-scale Breach mode, the first two phases revolve around escorting or halting a battering ram.

Recent findings suggest that introduced with the Marching Fire expansion in October 2018, Breach completely changes its structure once the ram breaks through both gates. At that point, the ram disappears and the match transforms into an asymmetrical raid with limited respawn tickets, forcing the attacking team to coordinate and take down an AI-controlled Commander with massive health and area-of-effect attacks while defenders fight to keep him alive—turning tactical skirmishes into a high-stakes team raid.

Originally released in arcades in 1996 before finally reaching modern consoles and PC in 2022 via Capcom Fighting Collection, although it's one of those games from the Japanese company that desperately needs a remake. Red Earth (known as Warzard in Japan) took a wildly unconventional approach to the genre. Rather than pitting you against a traditional lineup of rival fighters, it built its main Quest Mode around full-fledged RPG progression.

It kicks off like a classic Capcom 2D fighter with a striking dark-fantasy aesthetic, letting you choose from four heroes, before rapidly shifting into a boss-rush RPG. As you clear battles, your character earns experience, levels up, unlocks new special moves, and picks up elemental orbs and weapons off the ground to survive multi-phase encounters against towering monsters that mutate and change their attack patterns mid-fight.

In a recent development, super Smash Bros. Brawl remains a beloved favorite for many fans, and its main campaign pulled off a full-blown genre switch in its second act. Throughout the first half of The Subspace Emissary, the mode plays like a linear, side-scrolling beat 'em up broken into distinct stages with rotating pairs of heroes—a straightforward formula I genuinely enjoyed.

According to recent reports, however, once the roster finally unites in Subspace and suffers a crushing defeat at the hands of Tabuu, the entire mode transforms into The Great Maze. Suddenly, those linear stages give way to a massive, interconnected, non-linear Metroidvania-style map where you command the entire unlocked roster, rescue captured trophies, and backtrack through merged zones to rematch bosses—a sudden shift in structure that completely caught me off guard back in the day.

Recent findings suggest that when it comes to fighting games that radically reinvent themselves halfway through, Soulcalibur III takes the crown. On the surface, it serves as the direct follow-up to Soulcalibur II's fast-paced, 3D weapon-based combat built around smooth 8-Way Run movement—familiar territory for anyone who loved the series on PlayStation 2.

Inside its signature Chronicles of the Sword campaign, however, the game fuses traditional one-on-one weapon duels with a real-time strategy game. You command squads across a tactical map, capture strongholds, and level up custom-built units—and by the second half of the campaign, early small-scale skirmishes escalate into complex, multi-front sieges against iconic series veterans and high-level bosses that test both your strategic planning and your blade skills.

Marteen still finished VCT EMEA Stage 2 as the team’s top-rated player, with a rating of 1.23. Fnatic’s own 2026 campaign ended earlier than planned. Joblife knocked them out with a 2–0 win in the VCT EMEA Stage 2 Play-Ins.

The signing follows a clear-out of long-serving players. Boaster had been with Fnatic since 3 February 2021. Alfajer arrived on 9 May 2022, and crashies on 11 December 2024.

Marteen’s own spell at Gentle Mates ran from 20 November 2025 to 25 October 2026. The two rosters are now tied together by the same transfer window.

Gentle Mates had already cleared their own decks. All five players on the active roster and both coaches were let go before the club’s first season as a VCT partner team.

In a recent development, for a British organisation, the swap leaves Fnatic’s identity in new hands. Boaster had been the longest-serving name in the departing group. Kaajak and Cloud are now the continuity, with marteen as the headline addition.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game. The twist is that the specs not only include useful information for PC players, they also cover similarly relevant details for console players, who traditionally don’t get mentioned in those reveals.

The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.

On the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG. Each set indicates the graphics preset being used - and crucially, the resolution and framerate targets you can expect with each.

In a recent development, with the exception of the Minimum spec, all other presets do not appear to rely on upscaling of any kind. They do not say, however, whether ray tracing is being used with any of them, which is a feature that will throw all of those specs out of whack.

That same transparency also extends to non-PC platforms, which traditionally get few, if any, details about their own resolution and framerate targets. The console set of specs are extensive, just like PC, covering both PlayStation, and Xbox.

According to recent reports, it’s granular enough to indicate which upscaling tech is being used, where applicable. This is relevant for owners of a PS5 Pro, a console that has access to Sony’s PSSR upscaling, alongside the standard AMD FSR tech the base console - and Xbox - use.

The developer has also revealed the base resolution for each mode across each console, and the resolution the image will be upscaled to using whichever tech is being utilised.

In a recent development, and, if you’re one of the five people who play games on Mac, you’ll be thrilled to know that the specs also include a section for Mac devices, split between the different Mac chips. The quality preset being used with each is not clear, however.

Finally, there's a set of specs for the Rog Xbox Ally, covering both the X and S models.

Sources indicate that crimson Desert arrives March 20 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. You can expect more coverage from us at release and beyond.

When you think about GTA as a series, the first thing that probably comes to mind is driving through crowds of people, gunning down whoever you like, just generally doing crime without any care in the world. I wouldn't exactly call it an empathy game, not to say that other games are any better at such a thing anyway. But with GTA 6 out, crikey, next bloody week, a newly introduced interview has gone up with co-studio head Rob Nelson where he shared that you have a bit more space to be empathetic compared to previous entries.

Sources indicate that "Crime is a fundamental part of GTA - at least up until now, it has been," Nelson told The Guardian (via @GameRoll_, ta IGN) in a new interview. "We're trying to make sure we're not punishing people for playing the game they are used to … [but] your actions will have some effect on how the game plays out." When asked about whether this will be the first GTA game to encourage people to be empathetic, Nelson responded, "I would say so. I would say that it's a product of the story we're trying to tell. We've tried for the first time in a GTA to provide mechanisms that encourage it, for those who want to.".

I am deeply curious as to what those mechanics may be, given that most of what we've seen so far is pretty relegated to shootin', lootin' and a bit of smoochin'. If you steal a car, is there an NPC that loses their job because of it? Can you repair the harm you caused through that action? I'm sure hardly anyone else that's vibrating through their skin in excitement for almost having the game in their fingertips will be asking such questions, I'm just often wary of empathy mechanics in games.

Sources indicate that in any case, doesn't matter all that much for us PC lot just yet, especially because Rockstar are preparing themselves both legally and technically to tackle pirated copies of the game. Rockstar will obviously be quite busy at the moment too, not just because of that whole launching a game thing, but because UK-based workers will be voting to unionise as we speak. If formed, it could be 1600 members strong, which would make it the biggest games union in the UK. Solidarity with all the workers as the voting process continues. I hope you get the result you deserve.

💡 Key Takeaways
