  • It has been revealed that as you no doubt know by now, GTA 6 is absolutely chock-a-block with references to other video games.
  • Industry observers note that so far, one such series is Kingdom Hearts, which is a little bit of a shame since it’s my all-time favourite.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some Kingdom Hearts fans are convinced that they’ve found a reference to the series in Grand Theft Auto 6, but not everyone is so sure it's intentional.

It has been revealed that as you no doubt know by now, GTA 6 is absolutely chock-a-block with references to other video games. We’ve seen Mario, Final Fantasy, the original Vice City, Clair Obscur, a surprisingly sharp The Last of Us jab, and oh so much more. In fact, it’s probably easier to say the games that don’t have some kind of easter egg in GTA 6.

Industry observers note that so far, one such series is Kingdom Hearts, which is a little bit of a shame since it’s my all-time favourite. You’d think a Keyblade ripoff would be hiding somewhere in Leonida, but that doesn’t appear to be the case just yet. Even if the series’ signature weapon isn't lurking, some fans are sure there’s a nod in there to one of its iconic symbols.

Industry observers note that as pointed out by Redditor Vogcoycoycut on the Kingdom Hearts subreddit, fans have found what they believe to be a reference to the series within GTA 6. It can be found during one of the game’s story missions, where Jason and Dre’Quan go to a watch store that’s clearly meant to be parodying Rolex.

Industry observers note that on the floor of that shop is a crown symbol that’s meant to be riffing on the one that Rolex has. Only, in this case, it’s much closer to the crown featured on Sora’s necklace and serves as one of Kingdom Hearts' main symbols. It’s not one-to-one or anything, but it’s incredibly close, and much more so than a generic crown logo.

While the riff on Rolex and the symbol being featured in a jewellery store (which makes me think of Sora’s necklace) do make it seem like a nod to Kingdom Hearts, there’s also a chance that it’s just a generic crown symbol that’s close to KH and that fans are seeing what they want to see. The thread is clearly very split on whether it’s intentional or not, and I can't blame them.

You could even really stretch by saying that time is a reference to Young Xehanort. Like I say, you’d REALLY be stretching.

That being said, this is Rockstar that we’re talking about, so we know that no detail is included in GTA 6 without at least some thought behind it. It’s still certainly not definitive, but there’s a chance someone at the studio is a big fan of Kingdom Hearts and wanted to include at least one nod to the series.

Battlefield 6 is getting a free trial next week with a decent selection of maps and modes

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Battlefield Studios has declared that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week.
  • Though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous.
  • For starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield Studios has declared that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week. Well, a portion of the game is, anyway, as part of a free trial that will include some of the game’s most popular modes and maps.

Though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous. Here’s what to expect.

For starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24. The trial will be accessible from Battlefield Redsec, the already free-to-play portion of the game.

Once downloaded, you’ll find a new Battlefield 6 Free Trial section in the main menu. Because Redsec and Battlefield 6 multiplayer share progression, if you played the former at any point, you’ll be able to pick up from where you left off.

The same is also true the other way around; if this is your first time with Battlefield 6, all your unlocks will carry over to the full version, as well as to Redsec if you decide stick with the free-to-play off-shoot.

Once it kicks off, you’ll find three playlists to choose from. Casual Breakthrough, All-out Warfare, and a third playlist showcasing the latest Nightfall game mode and its associated map.

All-out Warfare is what you come to Battlefield for, and that playlist features Conquest, Breakthrough, as well as BF6’s newcomer Escalation - all large-scale, combined arms game modes. They will be playable across four maps. You get to play on two from Season 2: Contaminated, and Hagental Base, one from Season 1: Eastwood, and Mirak Valley from the base game.

According to recent reports, casual Breakthrough is based on a playlist that already exists in the core game, and it’s really designed as a nice on-ramp for newly introduced players. It also offers less intense gameplay, perfect for people grinding unlocks.

Industry observers note that casual Breakthrough is limited to just 16 real players (eight per team), with the rest filled up with bots. You earn the same amount of XP in those matches, except when you interact with bots, so killing a bot will net less than a human player. Outside of that, unlocks, Challenges and all other things that don’t depend on stat-tracking can be done within.

In the trial, the Casual Breakthrough playlist includes Hagental Base, Contaminated, and Eastwood.

The most interesting is the third playlist, in part because its content will also be available to owners of the full game for the first time right alongside free-to-play players. Nightfall is a playlist exclusive to the Hagental Base map.

This is a very small map, so the mode selection here is Team Deathmatch, Squad Deathmatch, and Domination. Under Nightfall conditions, lights across the entire map are turned off, so you’re going to have use your NVGs to be able to see. This is also a god opportunity to try out weapon attachments that specifically work under low-light conditions, which typically don’t get much use in multiplayer.

March 17 also marks the launch of the second stage of Battlefield 6’s Season 2, which comes with the aforementioned Nightfall content, as well as a substantial new revision - so the timing works out nicely for everyone.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • To say that it is just straight up Dark Souls combat would be unfair, from the looks of things.
  • You can take part in matches with up to eight people, which presumably extends to AI (not that kind) enemies too, in "atmospheric duels, clashes, deathmatches and more." It looks neat!

It has been revealed that the idea of Dark Souls PvP has always scared me a tad. You can replace Dark Souls with Bloodborne or Elden Ring, I've typically just been a coward when it comes to the idea of fighting another, real person. They're probably going to be better than me! I don't use tactics in Souls games, I use brute force until I get my way! That being noted, I do have to admit I quite like the look of Rasen, a game that is essentially just the PvP component of Dark Souls (or PvE if you just want to take on some computer-controlled enemies) that just launched into early access.

To say that it is just straight up Dark Souls combat would be unfair, from the looks of things. For one, it looks more like it leans a tad towards Sekiro with a blades-only kind of affair, whether that be big or small. And blades a plenty they have, ranging from your classic sword, to scythes, to halberds and all sorts. It's a much flashier looking affair too, with fancy slashing effects that seem to buff moves and a pace that seems much faster than Souls games tend to be.

You can take part in matches with up to eight people, which presumably extends to AI (not that kind) enemies too, in "atmospheric duels, clashes, deathmatches and more." It looks neat! And best of all, unusually for a 3D arena fighter, it has rollback netcode. For those unfamiliar, and to try and explain it simply, this is essentially a bit of tech you'll find in predominantly 2D fighting games that predicts every possible input you could make in a given moment, helping to reduce lag time and allow for tighter matches (and less rage quitting).

Industry observers note that that's a bit harder to do in a 3D environment given that you have a lot more options at your disposal when it comes to movement, so if it works that's some impressive stuff! And we could all quite easily find out together, as a demo for Rasen is available to try out. Or, alternatively, you can just pick it up whole hog on Steam right now, as it's available in early access.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A new Honkai: Star Rail Special Program has concluded, which means some fresh news about the game’s upcoming major enhancement. Version 4.1, unveiled today as Unraveled for Daybreak, is the action RPG’s next moment, kicking off on March 25.

In a recent development, unraveled for Daybreak is the next chapter in the ongoing story of Planarcadia, with the Astra Express Crew now invited to a fan fest inspired by their own past journeys. The aptly named Star Rail Fest is ostensibly hosted to allow more of the citizens of Arcadia to experience the Trailblaze.

In a recent development, as everyone’s eyes is fixated on the grand Star Rail Fest, the Phantasmoon Games continue to be in full swing, as does the war with the Supplicants. Star Rail Fest is, however, the major focus of this enhancement, in case it wasn't obvious.

The event is made up of three large-scale zones, each themed around past excursions of the Astral Express. You’ll get to explore the Belobog Zone, Xianzhou Luofu Zone, and Penacony Zone. Later on, you’ll also be able to visit Pearluxe Tower, the headquarters of Pearluxe Corp.

Each area will feature its own attractions, such as the balloon figures of Supreme Guardian Cocolia and the Destruction Engine, the duel against the Lord Ravager Phantylia at Scalegorge Waterscape, and the Pearluxe Tower’s Alloy King Pom-Pom model.

The hot upcoming arrival is bumbling noirish detective Ashveil whom we've met in Version 4.0, and who becomes a playable character with this revision. Ashveil is a 5-Star Lightning-Type character, on the Path of The Hunt. You’ll be able to pull for him throughout 4.1's runtime, which is slightly reduced at four weeks instead of the usual six, in order to rebalance the schedule after the extra-long Version 3.8.

In combat, Ashveil is capable of increasing Crit Damage of all allies. He can also mark an enemy as Bait, which reduces the Defence of all enemies on the field so long as this tag holds. If Ashveil uses his Skill on the baited target, he will deal extra Damage and regain Skill Points for the team.

It has been revealed that ashveil can bully that baited target even further by launching Hounding Pursuit. If any of his teammates attacks the Bait, he can further deliver a follow-up attack that gradually accumulates Gluttony for as long as he’s in combat. Gluttony can later be consumed to boost follow-up attack damage.

According to recent reports, if he lands a kill, Ashveil continues to deal damage to the next enemy he attacks. That buff is transferred if that enemy is killed. Even in map exploration, Ashveil can be deadly, capable of inflicting Stunned upon enemies within a specific range.

Sources indicate that returning characters this patch will be Hyacine in the first half, and Boothill in the second half. Once again, due to the reduced runtime, their banner reruns will be slightly shorter than normal, at just two weeks each instead of three — so be sure to take that into account if you're planning on pulling for either of them.

Version 4.1 also adds the Wispae War Saga, a new activity where you can practice your leadership skills by commanding different types of Wispae Soldiers in the Graphia Academy. You can upgrade each one, use spell cards to alter their effects, and later face other champions. You ultimately want to play this to unlock new Wispae Companions, not to mention complete the challenges within.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, I have always been enamored with the different ways that games have been brought to life, and Mods in particular have always felt magical to me.
  • In a recent development, the same goes for bonus modes and custom maps that were never meant to be more than a fun extra.
  • Right, before you are all coming for me with pitchforks: Gwent never actually became bigger than The Witcher 3, and I have no qualms about admitting that straight away.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, I have always been enamored with the different ways that games have been brought to life, and Mods in particular have always felt magical to me. Someone, somewhere, loves a game so much that they start tinkering with it in their free time. Every now and then, that little side project ends up taking on a life of its own. Some of the biggest games in the world, including two of the biggest esports I write about, started out exactly like that.

In a recent development, the same goes for bonus modes and custom maps that were never meant to be more than a fun extra. A few devs probably thought it would be fun to include a little bit of an extra to fans, or had an idea with limited resources that they wanted to give a try. Some of them went on to get their own releases, others created entire genres, and a few of them quite frankly outshone the game they were tucked away in. And in the spirit of that, let's take a look at ten side modes that became bigger than the game they came from.

Right, before you are all coming for me with pitchforks: Gwent never actually became bigger than The Witcher 3, and I have no qualms about admitting that straight away. Very few things could. The hype around it was something else, though: people happily ignored the end of the world to sit in taverns and play cards with every merchant, blacksmith and innkeeper they came across, and CD Projekt Red clearly noticed.

Sources indicate that the standalone version, GWENT: The Witcher Card Game, is something fans eagerly awaited. It did, however, come with its own sets of concerns. The version of Gwent it delivered displayed a few stark differences to the version people knew and fell in love with: It was free-to-play, quite competitive, and ultimately, a lot of fans simply never warmed to it. If you're after that original feeling, most people will point you towards Thronebreaker: The Witcher Tales instead.

In a recent development, still, a card game from inside an RPG becoming popular enough to get its own release almost never happens. CD Projekt Red supported it until the end of 2023, and even then, it handed the game over to the community rather than switching it off. It didn't quite live up to the hype, but it absolutely earned its place on this list.

The Stanley Parable really shouldn't work as well as it does. You're an office worker, a narrator tells you exactly what you're doing, and it's up to you whether you want to listen to him. It's one of the funniest games I know, and it started out as a free Half-Life 2 mod that Davey Wreden released in 2011.

Recent findings suggest that wreden wanted to play around with what storytelling in games could be, and it clearly struck a nerve: the mod was downloaded more than 90,000 times in just two weeks. William Pugh then reached out about turning it into something bigger, and the two of them spent the next two years working on it entirely online. They only met in person a month after it came out, which is a detail to the origin story that I personally find quite charming.

That remake released in 2013 and sold over 100,000 copies within a matter of days. Ultra Deluxe followed in 2022 and did the same within 24 hours.

Team Fortress 2 is so closely tied to Valve that it's easy to forget it didn't start there at all. It began as a Quake mod in 1996, made by three Australians, Robin Walker, John Cook and Ian Caughley, who had been inspired by a little Doom map they came across at LAN parties. Two teams, a bunch of very different classes, and everyone has a job to do. Sound familiar?

Industry observers note that valve liked it so much that it bought the rights and offered its creators jobs. Caughley said no, but Walker and Cook moved over, and Team Fortress Classic came out in 1999 as a mod for Half-Life. It then took until 2007 for Team Fortress 2 to finally arrive, with a cartoony art style that has aged better than most games from that year.

It has been revealed that once it went free-to-play in 2011, it became bigger and better. Somewhere between capturing the intelligence and pushing the payload, a huge part of the community became very, very invested in hats. I'm not judging, but I am a little bit scared of how much money has gone into them.

In a recent development, as someone who writes about esports, the lore behind Dota is one of my favorite tidbits of the gaming world. It all started with Aeon of Strife, a custom StarCraft map, which inspired a modder called Eul to make Defense of the Ancients for Warcraft III all the way back in 2003. Eventually, Eul made it open-source, and from there, it passed from hand to hand.

It has been revealed that the most popular version became DotA Allstars, made by Steve "Guinsoo" Feak, and when he moved on, the mysterious IceFrog took over. Guinsoo went on to help create League of Legends, which means one Warcraft III map is responsible for two of the biggest esports on the planet. What a wild family tree!

Valve hired IceFrog in 2009, Dota 2 came out in July 2013, and the rest is happily ever after: it has been one of the most played games on Steam ever since. Truth be told, I love that the person who has shaped Dota more than anyone is still somewhat of a mystery. Somehow, that makes the whole thing even more feel like classic Dota.

Counter-Strike is one of the most influential FPS games ever created, but it doubled as probably the most impressive job application to exist. Minh "Gooseman" Le was in his last semester at university and wanted something that would help him get into game development, so he started working on a mod for Half-Life. Jess "Cliffe" Cliffe ran the website and the community, and the first beta came out in June 1999.

Industry observers note that every new beta brought in more players, and by 2000, Valve had bought the rights and hired them both. From there, it was Source, Global Offensive and, in 2023, Counter-Strike 2, with the series becoming one of the biggest esports in the world along the way. Its Majors are still some of the biggest events in esports.

Industry observers note that counter-Strike 2 still regularly sits at the very top of Steam's charts, with over 30 million monthly players. Gooseman, for the record, definitely got the job. I'd say it worked out.

There was a point where it felt like every other game had zombies in it, and DayZ was right at the heart of that. It started out in 2012 as a mod for Arma 2, made by Dean "Rocket" Hall, and threw you into a huge open world full of the undead. The zombies were never really the scary part, though: other players were, because you never knew whether the person waving at you wanted to team up or take your tinned food.

You needed Arma 2 to play the mod, so its popularity sent a three-year-old military sim right back to the top of Steam's charts. It reached a million players within four months, Hall joined Bohemia Interactive, and work began on a standalone version. Bohemia, quite understandably, was delighted.

That version launched into Early Access in December 2013 and sold over two million copies in under six months, before its full release in 2018. I'll say this much: it hasn't moved all that far away from the mod, and that is a good thing. If you like survival games and don't mind a bit of betrayal, it's well worth your time.

I’ll be honest, most of the Skyrim mods I personally perused have always been about silly things like turning every dragon into Thomas the Tank Engine. Those of you with more dignified taste, however, might be aware of The Forgotten City. It’s a time-travelling murder mystery set in an ancient underground city. Nick Pearce spent more than 1,700 hours on it, and it clearly was time well spent: the mod had over three million downloads, and an Australian Writers' Guild Award, the first time a video game had ever won one.

Pearce quit his job as a lawyer and rebuilt it as a standalone game with two other developers. It moved from Skyrim to ancient Rome, but kept its central idea: there is one rule, and if anyone breaks it, everybody pays. Steal from someone or hurt them, and the entire city is turned into gold.

Sources indicate that luckily, you get sent back to the start of the day whenever that happens, with everything you've collected so far. It's almost roguelike in that way, and every loop teaches you a little more about the people around you. I think it's one of the best detective games out there, and it started its life as a Skyrim mod.

Call of Duty: World at War was a very serious entry about the Pacific front of World War II, which is exactly why it's so funny that most people remember it for zombies. Treyarch hid Nacht der Untoten at the end of the campaign as an Easter egg, with no marketing behind it at all. You finished the story, and suddenly you were boarding up windows in a bunker whilst zombies tried to get in.

It was a hit straight away, so every map pack after that came with a newly introduced Zombies map. The first map didn't even have a story, but fans started building one anyway, and Treyarch eventually leaned all the way into it. The result is one of the most convoluted storylines in gaming, spread across multiple Black Ops games.

Recent findings suggest that zombies has been part of nearly every Call of Duty since, and these days, it's not unusual for it to be the main reason people pick up a Treyarch game at all. Quite the career for an Easter egg. Not even the developers saw that one coming.

It has been revealed that dota Auto Chess is the youngest entry on this list, and boy, did it blow up fast. Drodo Studio released it as a custom game inside Dota 2 in January 2019. You put Dota heroes on a chessboard, combine them to make them stronger and then sit back whilst they fight on their own, and the developers have actually said that Mahjong was a substantial inspiration.

Within months, it had over eight million players, and the big studios very rapidly wanted a piece of it. Valve made Dota Underlords, Riot added Teamfight Tactics to League of Legends, and Blizzard brought Battlegrounds to Hearthstone. Drodo Studio, meanwhile, released its own standalone Auto Chess.

Industry observers note that the hype has calmed down since then, but the auto battler genre is still very much here, and all of it traces back to one custom game. I find it quite funny that one of the biggest gaming trends of 2019 started out as just another option in Dota 2's custom games menu. Never underestimate a menu.

Industry observers note that the Binding of Isaac has a truly baffling amount of mods, and as someone that used to be utterly besotted with both the OG as well as The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth, I have tried a large amount of them. A lot of them were high quality, but Antibirth was something else. Released by a group of fans in December 2016, it was basically an entire expansion: thousands of fresh rooms, nearly 100 new items and even its own soundtrack. It felt so much like Isaac that it was hard to believe it wasn't official.

Edmund McMillen clearly shared the fans’ feelings. He loved how well it understood the themes and style of his game, and rather than ignoring it, he started working with the team behind it. In 2018, he confirmed The Binding of Isaac: Repentance, the final DLC for the game, built on Antibirth.

In a recent development, repentance introduced in 2021, with the Antibirth team helping to make their mod official, alongside a whole lot of fresh content. I love that a fan project ended up becoming the final chapter of the game it was made for. Not many modders can say that.

Recent findings suggest that if a game is about cooking, at minimum I'll have to give it a quick testspin. Outside of this whole writing about video games thing, my other lot in life is soul bound to food, so I'm always curious to see how the two can be mixed together. And earlier this week, The Snackbar at the End of the World was revealed, a wonderfully cartoonish action-adventure game set in a magical, slightly post-apocalyptic version of 1960s Italy where you go out and forage for ingredients while fending off monstrous crops before turning them into tasty meals back in your struggling restaurant.

First up, I just have to gush over the artstyle a bit. The whole game is hand-drawn with a colourful, comic book look that has an impressive sense of depth to it. It gives off a deep love of Italian architecture and landscapes, and that admiration clearly extends to the food too. Once you've gotten the ingredients you need, you then, loosely in the vein of Cooking Mama, prepare them and make various classic Italian dishes by performing some quick minigames. Simple, but charming! The rest of the time you're off killing some ghoulies that look like mutated fruit and veggies, with the occasional fungus-possessed hog and, uh, haunted statues? I think?

I'm also quite pleased about two points made on the game's Steam page. First is the content description: "This game features cartoon violence, sensitive political themes set in a fictional world, and depictions of an oppressive government committing crimes against its citizens." There is clearly a romantic quality to the game and I'd be worried if it didn't acknowledge any of the political context of the decades preceding.

Sources indicate that the other line reads, "Every sound effect, musical note, design decision, and line of code is human-made. Because this game is about human relationships and delicious food – and that’s not a story we would ever trust AI to tell." Thank the lord! Right now there's no release date attached to The Snackbar at the End of the World, unsurprising given it was only revealed this week. But while we all wait for a date, you could perhaps join me in throwing it a wishlist on Steam.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that hoYoverse has delivered another Special Program for the second day running, this time for Zenless Zone Zero. The developer revealed the full details of Version 2.7, subtitled Champions Never Fall to the Past.

This next major update arrives March 24, adding two latest Agents, and introducing the Hollow Champion competition.

According to recent reports, most things in Version 2.7 follow on from the Hollow Champion competition, which brings together old friends and familiar faces, as well interesting newcomers. Everyone is in it to win some major rewards and earn glory.

In a recent development, among the unexpected participants the competition has attracted are the Public Security's Metropolitan Order Division, and even some former Calydon's Sweepers. A big challenge that awaits is Black Wolf Romeul, who’s capable of increasing his Crit Damage Resistance and Interruption Resistance by activating a Corruptive Barrier.

Romeul can also cause enemies to continuously lose HP, but you can beat him by putting together a squad that can deal sustained Anomaly damage, which will break through the barrier swiftly.

Our first new arrival in Version 2.7 is Cissia of the Metropolitan Order Division. She is an S-Rank Electric Attack Agent who automatically gains three stacks of Venom when she enters the battle. Each stack deals Electric Damage while also increasing her Crit Rate for a time.

When she runs out of Venom, which will happen, Cissia can generate more stacks by using her EX Special Attack. She can also use her Basic Attack, Serpent's Kiss, to better utilise the fresh stacks of Venom she generates.

The other newly introduced Agent may be the more exciting. Nangong Yu, the captain and lead dancer of the Angels of Delusion, can now be part of your team. Nangong Yu is an S-Rank Ether Stun Agent who can boost her team’s Anomaly Buildup Rate against Stunned enemies.

It has been revealed that being part of an idol group has its perks, because she automatically regenerates Downbeat as time goes on, and even more any time a squad member inflicts an enemy with Anomaly. Nangong Yu can then use Downbeat - after enough has been accumulated - on charged attacks that keep enemies stunned for longer. Her Ultimate triggers Ether Veil: Delusion Reprise, which boosts the entire squad’s Attack.

Returning Agents in Version 2.7 will be Yidhari, the S-Rank Ice Rupture Agent, as well as Seed, the Electric Attack Agent.

According to recent reports, outside of all the very vital action in the core story, this chapter also brings new themed events to Lumina Square’s Simmer Hot Pot Restaurant. The Simulated Battle Trial is also getting some love, with updated mechanics and new enemy line-ups.

Catch up on our recently updated Zenless Zone Zero character tier list, and don’t forget to check out these Zenless Zone Zero codes before you jump in for some free stuff.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, while following a peculiar trail of silver and saffron leaves around the largest roots of the Treehouse, you come across a hexagonal wooden door lying half-hidden among ivy and moss. Scraping away the dirt, you discover a faint, absurd engraving of a newspaper. What mystery is here? You turn the brass knob – strange, it is warm! – and the engraving of the newspaper flutters. The pages turn faster and faster, emitting a howling gale that bowls you head over foot. When you pick yourself up, you are inside a vast attic full of books and bricabrac, lit from one side by windows that offer no view of the outside world – just light and mist.

Tarnation! You have been lured into the eternal prison of Sunday Afternoon. Fortunately, there are several ways to escape. Each of the arcane objects before you is secretly a portal, transporting you to another site of arcane activity, in a bizarre web of diversions that cannot possibly reflect the hand of a human curator. Which will you choose?

As you step forward, your toe nudges an ornamental scroll. It growls and wriggles like a panicking caterpillar, scooting away under a table. Before you lose sight of it, you discern the title and subject of the text – it's an essay by Kyle Tam about the yokai of Promise Mascot Agency.

Deep in a drawer, you discover a sour-smelling binder full of extracts from an ancient and all but indecipherable dispute over the discovery of "generative AI" in something called "Big Walk". The stakes are long-buried, but many of the individual pieces of writing are lively. Here is Bruno Dias noting in passing that "one of the harms of the 'AI' political project is the propaganda machine dedicated to making you feel stupid and helpless." Here is a professorial interjection from Brendan Keogh calling on the warring parties to recognise when "critiques of generative AI are actually just deflected critiques of the capitalist relations of technology and labour". Here is Mike Cook arguing that "what's happening is not unusual, it's not extreme, it's not unfair and it's not a 'public flogging'." Here is a ticker tape message from Hannah Nicklin observing that "if your radical position doesn’t have room for transformation it will not be safe until it contains just you".

A footnote in the same dusty sheaf of papers points you towards another work from Mike Cook in a different drawer. This one consists of neon slides, slotted into an antique View-Master, and explores a comparison between procedural generation and street photography.

It has been revealed that peering at the weirdly white and opaque windowpanes, you realise there are intricate equations traced in the condensation. It appears to be a post-mortem for a "post-cosy" game called Danchi Days, in which developer Melos Han-Tani discusses wishlist conversion rates and the problem of not fitting neatly into any recognisable genre.

Recent findings suggest that A snowglobe stands on a mantelpiece, the flakes still orbiting a miniature washtub as though the object had been recently shaken, even though the chamber has clearly been abandoned for decades. You put it to your ear, anticipating the faint jingle of Xmas bells. Instead, you are almost deafened by a screeching guitar chord. Here is Erin Keane to explain.

Next to the snowglobe on the mantelpiece, there's a souvenir shop conch shell, polished to a high sheen. You put that to your ear, hoping to catch the soothing shuffle of surf on shingle, and a disembodied voice tells you to piss off. Tim Sniffen has some thoughts about gentrification, and why only he should be allowed to do it.

It has been revealed that again, one of these mystic artefacts hides the key to your release from the suffocating stillness of Sunday Afternoon. Which will you choose? Or have you, perhaps, brought a sorcerous teleportation device of your own? Please share. Here is Joanna Newsom's Cosmia to help you think.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 producer Rob Nelson has admitted that he was “praying” the game’s significant plot twist in Chapter 1 didn’t get spoiled ahead of time.

It has been revealed that leading up to the release of GTA 6, it felt like Rockstar had shown us plenty of what the game was about. We had a general idea of Jason and Lucia’s circumstances in Leonida, detailed reports on the game’s expanded mechanics, and enough footage of the world for some dedicated fans to piece together a mapping project.

According to recent reports, and, of course, there were the infamous Cyberleek leaks that indicated much more than Rockstar ever wanted us to. Now that the game is actually out, though, it’s painfully clear just how little we knew about GTA 6, which all starts in the game’s opening hour when perhaps its biggest plot point is revealed after years of hiding it away.

I’m sure anyone interested is already well past this point, but we’ll be discussing GTA 6’s main Chapter 1 twist below.

In a recent development, I am, of course, talking about the major reveal that Jason and Lucia have a child together, Tomas, who is taken away from them both after Lucia is arrested early on in the game. It’s as much of a surprise to Jason as it is to the players, as Rockstar somehow managed to keep it out of all the marketing and even didn’t get it ruined by Cyberleek.

VGC’s Jordan Middler recently had the chance to chat to Grand Theft Auto 6 producer Rob Nelson about that surprise moment. Nelson confirmed that Rockstar was “never” going to reveal that plot point, and that he was “praying it stays under wraps” before the game’s launch, especially with “everything that we’ve gone through”.

Nelson is surely referring to just how many leaks GTA 6 was hit with, which somehow didn't result in such a big point being spoiled.

Sources indicate that nelson went on to say that the twist is meant to shock the player, especially with how much everyone was speculating on Jason and Lucia’s relationship. Like with many of GTA 6’s elements, it’s also meant to take the game and your actions “in a completely different context”, and give you more to aim for than just money.

In a recent development, of course, while most players were surprised by Jason and Lucia being parents, it’s fair to say that there was at least some speculation about it. Many thought Ryan Gosling’s The Place Beyond the Pines, which has a similar leading duo with a child, was an inspiration point, but I don’t think anyone was certain Rockstar would follow through on such a substantial story focus.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As vibe coders desperately hurl commands at AI in an attempt to get GTA 6 running on PC, one former Destiny 2 dev claims it's led to the "most ridiculous dumpster fire ever" – one that, like a car crash, is hard to look away from.

Since notorious GTA 6 leaker Cyberleek dropped an Xbox build of the game last week – and more recently followed up with its executable file – multiple groups have been racing to get Rockstar's latest blockbuster up and running on PC. After all, it only launched on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, so there's a gap there for people without a console that folks have been desperate to fill – though I can't help but think that some hoping for their success might just be keen for a way to play GTA 6 for free.

Recent findings suggest that anyway, it was always inevitable that people would try this, but the way they've been going about it has been messy, to say the least. We've already observed vibe coders begging their AI models of choice to do the GTA 6 port for them, "make no mistakes," and do it "faster," and former gameplay capture artist at Bungie, Amy Hendricks, has also been watching on in dumbfounded awe, documenting what she calls "the most ridiculous dumpster fire ever" in a thread on Bluesky.

In a recent development, she first looks at "the slopfest" she calls Project Leonida – one of the frontrunning decompilation projects that yesterday saw its Discord server completely disappear after Rockstar apparently got in touch, and its 15-year-old lead quit (though they've since told followers to "ignore" those posts, so who knows what's going on there). Before that, Hendricks documented: "One group feels like the chatbot developers are not moving fast enough (One reason being the main dev is still at school), so they're going to split the main GTA 6 recomp team into two via forking.".

Sources indicate that not long after that, fears began that Rockstar and Take-Two were on the way. A screenshot Hendricks shares from the Discord server before its apparent takedown demonstrates users copy and pasting the same message they seemingly hoped would clear their name should any official investigation come about.

In a recent development, "In case of an investigation by any federal entity or similar, I do not have any involvement with this group or with the people in it, I do not know how I am here, probably added by a thrid party, I do not support any actions by the member of this group," they declare in unison. Yes, they all copied the same typos, too.

In a recent development, despite all this, though, the vibe coders pressed on. An amusing highlight demonstrates one asking the AI why its task was taking so long, to be patiently told by the robot, "Each rebuild takes a long time, and the hang fix changes the shaders too, so it would need another rebuild.".

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

Hendricks speculates that all these attempts are costing those involved some serious cash, too: "Fun fact: This is most likely using API Billing (Subs give you a small quota, API billing lets you go as far as your wallet allows), so everyone involved has most likely spent hundreds if not thousands of dollars already.".

A follow-up post further explains that one of the people streaming their vibe coding efforts was using Fable 5.2, and "API pricing is built around the price of 1 Million tokens. Fable charges $8 for input (what it does) and $40 output (what it puts out) per 1M. If he's been doing this day and night for hours, easily thousands of dollars.".

Oh dear. Needless to say, it's not looking like a smooth operation. As Hendricks puts it, "I have always wanted to see the supposed 'expert programmers with AI making recomps' in action and it turns out it's just a bunch of kids hitting their head on a wall so im gonna keep watching out of morbid [curiosity].".

In a recent development, despite it all, it does seem like progress is being made, though. One website – which Hendricks refers to as a "slop leaderboard" – is keeping track of the progress made across various unofficial GTA 6 PC projects, with the top one at the time of writing apparently 77.4% playable. I'm sure both prospective players and Rockstar alike will be watching this space with bated breath.

  • As shown off in the video above, CyberMP's not about being able to play through the base game's missions with friends, but rather cruise around Night City as a gang getting into races and PvP shootouts.
  • "After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders wrote on Discord.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After a couple of years of regular testing behind closed doors, Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta, giving anyone who fancies a bit of multi-merc action a chance to give it a go. Though, if you do, be prepared for bugs and crashes, as work on the mod is far from over with the release of this "true beta".

As shown off in the video above, CyberMP's not about being able to play through the base game's missions with friends, but rather cruise around Night City as a gang getting into races and PvP shootouts. In that regard, it seems more akin to GTA 4's online mode than GTA 5's, with classic improvised hijinks the main draw over being able to pull off gigs with a crew. Though, there do also look to be roleplaying servers which could scratch the itch of those more interested in pretending to be a merc than blowing up other people's rides.

"After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders wrote on Discord. "Anyone can jump in and play now — no invites or applications needed. Fair warning: this is a true beta. Crashes, desyncs, and server drops under heavy load are completely normal for now. That's exactly why we need testers. We welcome everyone: regular players, future server admins, and those who just love breaking game mechanics.".

It has been revealed that "Right now, our absolute priority is stability and fixing crashes," they continued later in the post. "New features are planned, but we need to polish the foundation first. A huge thank you to everyone who has been with us since the early versions, helped with closed testing, and patiently waited. We've finally reached this milestone. Let's see how the project handles real player traffic!".

According to recent reports, according to the modders, CyberMP's "client doesn't have a digital signature yet", which could cause antivirus software not to be a fan of it. They're also anticipating "problems with the anti‑cheat system", so it may be worth holding off on giving the mod a go if you're not keen on being trolled by someone with the sort of destructive power usually reserved for megacorps and AIs from beyond the blackwall in the Cyberpunkverse.

It has been revealed that for info on how to get CyberMP up and running, as well as create a custom server dedicated to the likes of roleplay or races, head over to its website. As you might expect, the mod requires a legit copy of Cyberpunk bought on either Steam, GOG, or the Epic store.

Nintendo Switch 2 Patent Paves Way For DS/Wii U Games

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (635 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A newly introduced set of Nintendo patents has been discovered that have paved the way for DS, 3DS, and Wii U games to return on Switch 2, so long as the player doesn’t mind shelling out for extra hardware.
  • The Nintendo DS was a massively popular system, selling 154 million units worldwide.
  • Recent findings suggest that one possible solution to Nintendo’s second screen problem may have been revealed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A newly introduced set of Nintendo patents has been discovered that have paved the way for DS, 3DS, and Wii U games to return on Switch 2, so long as the player doesn’t mind shelling out for extra hardware.

The Nintendo DS was a massively popular system, selling 154 million units worldwide. However, the system’s dual-screen design has made it hard for its titles to be rereleased on modern systems. Konami managed it with the Castlevania series, but few other companies seem interested in reviving their DS games on the Switch or Switch 2.

Recent findings suggest that one possible solution to Nintendo’s second screen problem may have been revealed. According to RetroDodo, two patents have been discovered that will allow the Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 to play games from the previous console generations.

Industry observers note that the first patent allows a game to be instantly transferred between two systems, while the second allows a different console to be used alongside one running a title, with the ability to use touchscreen controls. Taken together, these patents could emulate the Nintendo DS, 3DS, and Wii U GamePad.

Sources indicate that the caveat is that it would require someone to own two Nintendo Switch 2 units, or one of each Switch console, to run old games. This would be fine in a household that owns both systems, but for those who don’t, it’s an expensive proposition just to be able to run DS, 3DS, and Wii U titles.

Sources indicate that this isn’t the first time Nintendo has brought dual-screen games to consoles; DS games were available on the Wii U, with the GamePad used as the bottom screen. This isn’t the most elegant of solutions, especially as it forces the player to keep switching perspective between screens, but it gets the job done.

The caveat to these patents is that it would require someone owning two Nintendo Switch 2 units, or one of each Switch console, to run old games.

According to recent reports, there’s also the question of what games fans would even want to play on such a setup. The obvious answer is the Pokémon games, as fans would crawl through broken glass for modern ports of Pokémon HeartGold & SoulSilver that don’t cost hundreds of dollars on eBay. However, considering Game Freak seems averse to making money, there are still easier-to-port Pokémon games that aren’t on the Switch 2, and the DS games would take a ton of work to update.

It has been revealed that the Wii U also doesn’t have much, since pretty much all its best games are already on the Switch, and they received updated ports over the console’s lifespan. Sure, it’d be cool for Nintendo Land to return, but no one’s lining up for Star Fox Zero. The Wii U was such a bomb that Nintendo is unlikely to bring up its ghost, even through a costly hardware expansion.

Sources indicate that the Nintendo 3DS had a stacked library of amazing games, but some of them would lose the system's substantial selling point: 3D visuals. Super Mario 3D Land was a tremendous game, but it requires playing in 3D to get the full effect, especially for its stage secrets. The lack of Streepass and Spotpass would also take away a lot of the extra functions present in Nintendo 3DS games.

In a recent development, it’s entirely possible that these Nintendo Switch 2 patents won’t come to anything. After all, companies patent ideas all the time that never get made. The ability to play DS, 3DS, and Wii U games on the Switch 2 would be incredible, but the price of entry might be a bit too high for most fans, even if the titles are released for free on Nintendo Switch Online.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Nobody was hurt" in a shooting last week near the California office of Clockwork Revolution developers InXile, both the studio and local police have confirmed. The incident, which took place on November 11th, is presently being investigated and police have reportedly taken a suspect into custody.

Sources indicate that "Officers got there [on November 11th]," Tustin police sergeant Christopher Peterson mentioned in statement to Aftermath. "They responded to a report of a drive-by shooting there. Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt. Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why.".

It has been revealed that "We’re relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office," a spokesperson for InXile said in a separate statement. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate.".

Recent findings suggest that inXile are set to release steampunk RPG Clockwork Revolution next year. The studio, developers of the likes of Wasteland 3 and The Bard's Tale IV, are one of the few Xbox-owned studios not to have been affected - at least as of writing - by Microsoft's ongoing mass layoffs this year.

In a recent development, since being announced in 2023, Clockwork Revolution's dripped with Bioshock-ish vibes and popped up semi-regularly at Xbox showcases. "Wield the power of an incredible device to travel back in time, changing the past and rewriting the future of the city you call home: the vibrant steampunk metropolis of Avalon," reads its Steam synopsis. "In this immersive RPG, you'll step into the shoes of Morgan Vanette, a fully customizable player-character and member of the Rotten Row Hooligans. Travel between past and present as you battle the ruthless Lady Ironwood, who has been manipulating time to keep the working class struggling while amassing immense wealth and power.".

Best wishes to the staff at InXile, here's hoping that going forwards they're able to get with making what's looking to be an intriguingly funky game without enduring any more concerning incidents like this one.

If you want the very best offers, there are a couple of things I'd keep top of mind.

Use price comparison software: The most reliable way of making sure you're getting a good discount is using sites such as CamelCamelCamel. These track and report on a product's price history, including everything from record lows to average cost. That means you can quickly discern whether a saving is actually good or is just paying lip-service to the idea.

Beware of third-party knock-offs: I'm calling it now, the shelves are almost certainly going to be filled with knock-offs pretending to be something they're not. While I'm sure some of these are going to be worthy of attention, I'd avoid most nonetheless – there's no telling what their quality is going to be, and whether the product you're receiving is going to be anything like the one in promo shots. If in doubt, check user reviews or for official brand stores in the likes of Amazon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, crimson Desert, the open-world action RPG off-shoot from Korean MMO Black Desert Online, has officially rolled out, nearly six years after it was initially revealed. The game has been building up a lot of momentum over the years, which recently coalesced to turn it into one of 2026’s most anticipated titles.

All of it has been leading up to this moment, and the game appears to have landed smoothly, though not without controversy, as has seemingly become part of its MO.

In a recent development, it has not been 24 hours since Crimson Desert rolled out on PC and consoles, and it’s already become a massive hit. On Steam, one of two stores where the game can be purchased (the other being the Epic Games Store), the game shot to the top of the charts.

Sources indicate that the action RPG continued to accumulate more and more players on Steam, peaking at a very respectable 239,045 concurrent players (via SteamDB). Though its success was very much expected, we perhaps didn’t predict its peak would be that high.

Industry observers note that indeed, Crimson Desert has been in Steam’s top 100 global sellers list for six weeks, jumping up six spots to become the number one seller this week just before it debuted. As we get closer to the weekend, the numbers could climb even higher.

Sources indicate that this peak concurrent puts Crimson Desert in the same league as several of the other major releases of the first quarter of 2026. The top spot continues to belong to Slay the Spire 2, which peaked at a staggering 574,638 concurrent players. It happened just days after the juggernaut Resident Evil Requiem achieved its own 344,214 peak concurrent, which was the year’s highest up until Slay the Spire 2’s release. All three are well ahead of Nioh 3’s 88,045 peak concurrent, and Marathon’s nearly identical peak of 88,337.

Crimson Desert has seen something of a mixed reception by critics. James gave it three stars in our review, saying it “lacks the connective sinew to be truly functional,” which is a common criticism shared by other outlets. Many also lamented the sheer number of systems fighting for player attention, its poorly explained mechanics, and counterintuitive controls.

On Steam, at least, players have similarly been divided, with the current Steam user rating sitting at Mixed, based on 8,728 reviews. Unsurprisingly, most of the negative reactions fall on the clunky controls and the game’s tendency to, as one Steam user put it, “so miserably tries to be everything at once, and fails to be anything at all.”.

Industry observers note that if you’re just getting started in Crimson Desert yourself, or plan to do so soon, we recommend reading these crucial tips to help orient yourself in the game’s vast world. You should also plan your initial skill unlocks by prioritising these skills to spend your Abyss Artifacts first.

Star Wars: Galactic Racer launched on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC last month, and since then, players have taken a liking to Biddy Blas, completed hundreds of podraces, and more. More content is on the way, according to developer Fuse Games, which has revealed an upcoming "Speed Legends" update coming sometime next month.

In a recent development, more specifically, the free Speed Legends update will include private lobbies, input re-binding, two new podracers, eight podracing Scenarios, and more. This update also marks the first premium content: the M-68 Landspeeder Icon vehicle from Solo: A Star Wars Story and three premium speeders from Star Wars: The Mandalorian.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crimson Desert has been out for a few days now, and as positive as its been received by many players, the game suffers from several fundamental issues that anyone who’s played it has called out.

Perhaps the loudest one of those has been how the game controls, which is a problem that stems from the complexity of controls themselves, as well as the underlying animations behind many of the actions the player character performs.

In the first case, at least, something is being done.

According to recent reports, developer Pearl Abyss rolled out patch 1.00.03 for Crimson Desert on Monday. The patch is available now on Steam and PlayStation, with Xbox and the Epic Games Store following “at a later time.”.

Recent findings suggest that today’s update follows a letter to players the developer issued on Saturday. The letter generally acknowledged player feedback, but specifically pointed to complaints about the game’s clunky controls as something of a focus for the team.

In a recent development, the action RPG has actually broken its launch peak concurrent player numbers over the weekend, though only by a few thousands more. Its Steam user review rating has also improved over the same period.

It has been revealed that this latest update only includes an initial set of fixes, but Pearl Abyss vowed to keep working on addressing all other points of feedback. A highlight in 1.00.03 is the addition of a Storage at Howling Hill Camp, which can be used to store inventory items.

According to recent reports, the most key changes, of course, affect how the game controls on keyboard and mouse. Pearl Abyss included several fixes and altered some of the default presets to make the experience less painful when playing the game with a keyboard and mouse.

According to recent reports, there are sadly no changes to controllers, but it is something that the developer stated we can expect to see in future patches. More improvements for keyboard and mouse setups are in the works, too.

Beyond the control changes, patch 1.00.03 also includes a set of gameplay tweaks, especially when it comes to enemy health and difficulty. It also makes fast travelling more convenient, and brings a few fixes to NPC dialogue. You can read the full change log on Steam.

Industry observers note that if you’re deep in Crimson Desert already, we definitely recommend giving our guides a look. We recently added new pages to help you figure out where to socket your Abyss Gear, how to find Contribution Points - and where to spend them, as well as more generally helpful information like how to expand your inventory, and how to reveal the map.

Following the news of a Pokémon Champions balance patch enhancement, The Pokémon Company has now revealed some upcoming competitors are preparing to arrive in the free-to-play battle title.

On 2nd December 2026, Regulation Set M-D will see the arrival of Mega Heatran and Mega Tatsugiri. All up, there will be 24 newly added Pokémon available for battle and four more Mega Evolutions.

Here's the full announcement from the official Pokémon website:.

It has been revealed that some new competitors are preparing for battle! Regulation Set M-D will run in Pokémon Champions from Wednesday, December 2, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. PST to Wednesday, March 3, 2027, at 5:59 p.m. PST. - Go to Recruit. - Select Recruit Pokémon. - Select Roster Info.

- Mega Heatran has Water Compaction, which boosts its Defense by 2 Stages when hit by a Water-type Move - Mega Tatsugiri has a fresh Ability which increases its Special Attack by 1 stage when it enters battle.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A hacker has pleaded guilty to a number of online crimes, including the 2022 breach of Rockstar Games which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net.
  • The BBC report that, on November 16th, Arion Kurtaj pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar Games hack and a number of others he carried out with the hacking gang Lapsus$ while aged 16 and 17.
  • Industry observers note that kurtaj carried out the 2022 Rockstar hack while on bail for other hacking offences and being housed at a Travelodge hotel under police protection, the latter on account of rival hackers threatening to attack him over stolen Bitcoin stashes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A hacker has pleaded guilty to a number of online crimes, including the 2022 breach of Rockstar Games which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net.

The BBC report that, on November 16th, Arion Kurtaj pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar Games hack and a number of others he carried out with the hacking gang Lapsus$ while aged 16 and 17. Kurtaj, now aged 21, was previously sentenced to stay in a secure hospital indefinitely due to the severity of his autism, but was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial. He'll be sentenced at a later date.

Industry observers note that kurtaj carried out the 2022 Rockstar hack while on bail for other hacking offences and being housed at a Travelodge hotel under police protection, the latter on account of rival hackers threatening to attack him over stolen Bitcoin stashes. The Rockstar hack was reportedly done using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into the hotel room's TV, plus a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.

90 clips of unfinished GTA 6 were flung online by that hack, with Rockstar having refused to cooperate with Kurtaj's demand via an internal Slack channel that the organization contact him on massaging app Telegram within 24 hours. Rockstar claimed the breach cost them $5m million to recover from, in addition to staff having to waste thousands of hours.

Earlier this year, GTA 6 suffered yet another leak, with a hacker or hackers going by "Cyberleek" posting various videos of the game in action. Rockstar and parent tech giant Take-Two swiftly sprung into action, taking down videos, filing subpoenas, and issuing a statement that called the leak "heartbreaking".

Recent findings suggest that hopefully with the game's console release later this week, those will be the only two GTA 6 leaks which have to be added to the annals of gaming history. As much as marketing can leave a bad taste in the mouth, especially when it barely indicates anything of the actual product being advertised, neither of the GTA 6 leaks served much of a purpose beyond forcing people to waste some time and energy talking about the perpetrators.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that for a brief moment, Sauron ruled above all in The Rings of Power season 3, even likening his power to 'The One'.
  • Tolkien largely kept The One away from the machinations of Middle-earth in his works (free will still exists in this fantasy world), Eru Iluvatar is a fascinating figure that bears further examination.
  • Some spoilers for The Rings of Power season 3 ending follow.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that for a brief moment, Sauron ruled above all in The Rings of Power season 3, even likening his power to 'The One'. No, not the One Ring, but an even higher power – Eru Iluvatar, Middle-earth's answer to God.

Sources indicate that while J.R.R. Tolkien largely kept The One away from the machinations of Middle-earth in his works (free will still exists in this fantasy world), Eru Iluvatar is a fascinating figure that bears further examination. The deity will also likely factor into The Rings of Power season 4, so it's time to get a headstart on who exactly He is.

Some spoilers for The Rings of Power season 3 ending follow.

Eru Iluvatar – also known as The One – is the creator of the world of Arda and its continents, including Middle-earth.

While he manifested the literal space of Middle-earth, The One left it up to angelic beings known as the Ainur and Valar (themselves created by Eru) to sculpt the land and create life within it.

It has been revealed that eru Iluvatar rarely intervenes in matters in the world below, with the leader of the Ainur, Manwe, designated to – in effect – be his eyes and ears. Tolkien wrote of the godlike figure: "He was appointed to be, in the fullness of time, the first of all Kings: lord of the realm of Arda and ruler of all that dwell therein.".

Digging deeper into Tolkien's works reveals that Eru Iluvatar was planning to take mortal form in Middle-earth's Seventh Age. With Middle-earth actually being our planet, Tolkien lined up the years so Eru could feasibly be Jesus Christ. That idea only surfaced in a handful of correspondence, however, and never made it into the full literature. Even then, it's only an in-universe belief held by some religious observers.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

According to recent reports, as of The Rings of Power, Iluvatar is still worshipped as the one true God – especially in Numenor. Which makes Sauron's declaration that his power will make him stand above The One the worst possible sacrilege imaginable. So, will he descend from the heavens to ensure something is done? Well, about that….

Unless it deviates heavily from the source material, Eru Iluvatar will never show up – in a literal sense, anyway.

According to recent reports, spoilers for The Rings of Power season 4 follow, but with Sauron surrendering to Al-Pharazon, the Prime Video series is now on the path laid down by Tolkien, one which sees Numenor's ruler believing his power to be absolute. We won't go into specific details here, but Iluvatar does intervene at one point in one of Middle-earth's most shocking moments.

Eru's proxies and servants have also appeared in The Rings of Power. The Secret Fire, the power used by Iluvatar to create the world, appeared before Gandalf in season 3 and bestowed upon him the quest to unite once more with Pallando to help stop Sauron.

The Great Eagles have also turned up on multiple occasions, and they are emissaries of Iluvatar's right-hand angel Manwe and show up at moments of great importance.

All episodes of The Rings of Power season 3 is now streaming on Prime Video. For more to add to your watchlist, we have a collection of the best shows on Prime Video.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that one of the biggest reveals out of today’s Xbox Partner Preview showcase has been the fresh Stalker 2 expansion. The developer did tease some sort of announcement ahead of the event, but I don’t think an expansion was on many of our bingo cards.

Cost of Hope is the big news; a newly introduced add-on that the developer has wisely decided to reveal fairly close to release. Or, at least, the planned release target.

It has been revealed that first off, Cost of Hope is set for release this summer. It’ll arrive on all current platforms simultaneously, meaning PC, Xbox, and PlayStation. The expansion is described as “non-linear”, and it takes place in the heartlands, deeper into the Zone.

In a recent development, the story revolves around a conflict between Duty, and Freedom, two factions whose idea of the what the Zone is and their understanding of its possibilities differ widely. You’ll be playing as protagonist Skif once again, and the expansion’s events will run parallel to the main game.

In a recent development, GSC Game World notes Cost of Hope will introduce two new regions, offering dozens of hours of gameplay. We’ll get to actually explore the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant as part of the expansion, alongside the Iron Forest.

Recent findings suggest that each of the two new regions will have its own hub area, NPCs, quests, activities and stories. Of course, it wouldn’t be a Stalker expansion without some new weapons, and Cost of Hope promises a few - some can even be seen in the trailer.

It has been revealed that the developer also confirmed that there’s one other story DLC in the works. Together with Heart of Chornobyl, and Cost of Hope all three will form a trilogy of interconnected stories. More details on Cost of Hope - including a release date - will be revealed sometime in the summer.

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (890 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gameinformer ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: I Hate Video Game Romance – Here's Why Grand Theft Auto VI Is The Exception

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (890 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that generally speaking, I do not like romance mechanics in video games.
  • It has been revealed that if you've played Baldur's Gate 3, Stardew Valley, Date Everything, or practically any other game with romance options, you're familiar with the gameplay loop.
  • Many games structured like the ones above are written as well as they can be.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that generally speaking, I do not like romance mechanics in video games. I never find them convincing. Relationships build way too quickly, and usually all it takes to win someone over in an RPG or farming sim is a couple of conversations and a few gifts. In Grand Theft Auto VI, however, I'm extremely invested in the romance between Jason and Lucia, and it comes down to the game's quieter moments and slice-of-life mechanics.

It has been revealed that if you've played Baldur's Gate 3, Stardew Valley, Date Everything, or practically any other game with romance options, you're familiar with the gameplay loop. I ask an NPC about her hometown, sympathize with her tragic backstory, promise to be there for her, and then give her the book, cake, or mining resource she likes. Do it enough, and one day she'll approach me with the uncharacteristically heartfelt confession that she can't stop thinking about me. The process is too transparently mechanical: I can scan the dialogue options and instantly know which of the three sentences will boost my affinity rating the most. It feels less like an actual relationship and more like a long-term scheme to program someone into dating.

Many games structured like the ones above are written as well as they can be. The issue is scope and structure. Romantic relationships are nuanced and unique, but there often aren't enough resources during a game's development to represent more than the basic building blocks. Players are meant to suspend disbelief and fill in the gaps – even though you technically only spoke to that villager a few dozen times, you're married with a child, so you imagine it's actually been years.

Of course, this scope is the difference between Grand Theft Auto VI and these other games – Rockstar made time and space for everything in this world, and romance is no exception.

Since they're dating when the game begins, Jason and Lucia admittedly skip the courtship phase that many games focus on, but their relationship is still conditional and malleable – if you want them to like each other, you should be acting in their best interests. And while the mechanical aspect of their romance is still plenty visible, the actions to increase that meter are vastly expanded. There has been a lot of discussion about the early game, when you can prep for Lucia's release from prison by buying flowers or groceries, and while I like those gestures, they're not what sold me on the relationship. Say what you will about modern dating standards, but flowers and food are too easy – too obvious for me to feel connected to and invested in a couple.

Sources indicate that when I played this section, I felt like Jason's hair looked a little unkempt, so I got a shave and a haircut. And, to my surprise, this improved his relationship with Lucia. She wasn't around and wouldn't see the results until later, but it still scored me partner points, as did repairing the roof, painting the bedroom walls, and even giving Jason's car a new paint job. These unexpected, specific tasks don't just fill up the relationship gauge – they communicate information about both characters. Lucia is really looking forward to getting out of prison, and having a finished house and a clean, put-together partner sets her in a better mood. Meanwhile, my actions establish that my version of Jason knows she likes these things and would do them without even asking.

Minor, specific tasks like these are romantic because they imply a degree of thoughtfulness that sidesteps the grand gestures expected of a long-awaited reunion. Yes, there should be apples in the fridge, but that's a basic need; knowing the exact conditions Lucia wants the house to be in makes me believe Jason actually knows her. It becomes even more effective – both in real relationships and in the credibility of the in-game partnership – when thoughtfulness is demonstrated on a day-to-day basis, in the quiet moments.

Grand Theft Auto VI is a long game with a slow, steady pace, leaving room for the intimate interactions other games wouldn't have time for. If you come home at the end of the day and see your partner watching TV, you can sit next to them and get a bonus. When they go to sleep, they'll call out to you and ask you to lie in bed and scroll on your phone with them. You can hold hands in public, buy each other clothes, and remember to text back promptly. There are large, dramatic moments and professions of love, yes, but players are likely to experience vastly more of these minor interactions than those scripted cutscenes.

Sources indicate that romance can be flashy, but it has to be more than that. It's nice to see the starring duo dance, drive, and shoot at foes during cutscenes. But it's the long car rides when Lucia reassures Jason that her mom likes him, or the evening on the couch when Jason talks about how he likes the way Lucia laughs, that make this relationship work narratively.

Industry observers note that what are your favorite video game romances? Let us know in the comments!

Latest Update: Intel are being sued for "misleading" investors about "a massive glut of unwanted PC inventory" thanks to AI-fuelled price hikes

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that tech giant Intel are being taken to court for allegedly "misleading" their investors about the sheer scale of the impact of generative AI-fuelled component price hikes on PC sales.
  • All this follows Intel's last round of quarterly results, in which they declared a significant revenue fall; this triggered an Intel stock price drop from $92.07 per share on October 29th to $65.76 per share the next day, which this week's lawsuit characterises as "the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in over 50 years".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that tech giant Intel are being taken to court for allegedly "misleading" their investors about the sheer scale of the impact of generative AI-fuelled component price hikes on PC sales. The class action lawsuit in question claims that Intel's distribution and manufacturing partners have had to deal with "a massive glut of unwanted PC inventory", and that the gains from Intel's investments in AI datacenters aren't enough to make up for slowing sales of PCs to regular Josephines who just want fancy boxes they can play Deadlock on.

All this follows Intel's last round of quarterly results, in which they declared a significant revenue fall; this triggered an Intel stock price drop from $92.07 per share on October 29th to $65.76 per share the next day, which this week's lawsuit characterises as "the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in over 50 years".

In a recent development, the lawyers in question are from Robbins LLP, who specialise in "shareholder, whistleblower, antitrust, & consumer litigation". In a press release, they say they've filed suit on behalf of anybody who bought Intel stock from July 23rd to October 29th this year.

The suit claims that Intel neglected to tell investors that falling PC and component sales were having a "materially greater negative impact" on their third financial quarter 2026 Client Computing and Physical AI Groupresults than Intel had previously stated – to the tune of "hundreds of millions of dollars" in revenue shrinkage, compared to the previous quarter, with the situation still expected to "worsen".

They also accuse the organization of keeping schtum about the aforesaid "massive glut of unwanted PC inventory", together with the fact that "any positive impacts to Intel’s business and financial results resulting from data center construction and other aspects of the AI boom were more than offset by the negative effects on the Company’s business and financial results resulting from the PC market slowdown and the excess inventory buildup described above.".

Finally, they say Intel bosses have failed to disclose that they're struggling to procure an adequate supply of substrates – that is, materials used to create the base layer of chips, circuit boards and similar components. As such, the lawyers claim, Intel couldn't "ramp up production to meet data center CPU demand even if the Organization chose to divert production resources because of a slowdown in PC-related sales.".

Industry observers note that once the Godzilla of personal computing, Intel haven't been having a brilliant few years. Back in 2024, they recorded a multi-billion dollar quarterly loss, pushing then-CEO Pat Gelsinger to resign. As regards sales of gaming PCs, they've fallen behind AMD, though they've reportedly taken some ground back recently as regards desktop CPUs. As regards graphics cards, they have long been dwarfed by Nvidia.
